      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Re: Infra hiring — Senior/Staff Runtime engineer headcount and offer approval\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/gmail\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/gmail/laura_bennett/20260312-infra-hc-offer-approval-thread.json\nConnector: gmail\nWorkspace: laura_bennett\n\ncan expedite.\n\nI'll need signoff from Laura (People Ops) for the comp band and from Markus for team budget. Please reply with the level preference; I'll hold off contacting the recruiter until we have numbers.\n\nEvelyn\nEvelyn Hart\nDirector, Infrastructure\nRedwood Inference\n\nOn Sun, Mar 8, 2026 at 9:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:\n> Evelyn / Laura —\n> \n> Quick note to request headcount approval to hire a Senior/Staff runtime engineer focused on serving/runtime optimizations (KV cache, batching, kernel tuning).     "From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Req: Senior Infra Engineer (Runtime) — headcount & band request

Evelyn / Laura —

Quick note to request headcount approval to hire a Senior/Staff runtime engineer focused on serving/runtime optimizations (KV cache, batching, kernel tuning). Team has a clear blocker: the new quantized LLM pipeline increases token pressure and we need a dedicated hire to stabilize p99 latency and finish the kernel offload work.

Role: Runtime / Inference Infrastructure engineer
Level: hiring manager requests IC4/IC5 (Senior or Staff, flexible depending on candidate)
Suggested start: target onboarding 2026-05-01
Justification: shipping critical throughput improvements for Dedicated customers; several customer escalations tied to latency degradation under burst workloads.
Budget ask: propose comp band aligned to infra IC4-IC5 — rough guidance: base 185k–210k, target total comp 230k–300k depending on level and equity. Open to approve up to 275k total comp at upper bound if candidate has distributed systems + high-performance inference experience.

Please advise on band confirmation and whether we can convert an open headcount from Q2 hiring plan (infra pool) to this req. Attaching the JD in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
",
    "From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Req: Senior Infra Engineer (Runtime) — headcount & band request

Marcus —

Thanks for the write-up, this aligns with the infra priorities we discussed on the Q2 planning call. A few asks before I loop in TalentBridge to extend an offer:

- Confirm the preferred level (IC4 vs IC5) and the minimum acceptable total comp if we need to move quickly.
- Confirm which open headcount slot you want to use (infra pool vs platform dedicated slot).
- If we anticipate needing to go above the usual band, please put candidate-specific rationale here so I can expedite.

I'll need signoff from Laura (People Ops) for the comp band and from Markus for team budget. Please reply with the level preference; I'll hold off contacting the recruiter until we have numbers.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

> 
> Role: Runtime / Inference Infrastructure engineer
> Level: hiring manager requests IC4/IC5 (Senior or Staff, flexible depending on candidate)
> Suggested start: target onboarding 2026-05-01
> Justification: shipping critical throughput improvements for Dedicated customers; several customer escalations tied to latency degradation under burst workloads.
> Budget ask: propose comp band aligned to infra IC4-IC5 — rough guidance: base 185k–210k, target total comp 230k–300k depending on level and equity. Open to approve up to 275k total comp at upper bound if candidate has distributed systems + high-performance inference experience.
> 
> Please advise on band confirmation and whether we can convert an open headcount from Q2 hiring plan (infra pool) to this req. Attaching the JD in a follow-up.
> 
> Thanks,

    "From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Req: Senior Infra Engineer (Runtime) — headcount & band request

Evelyn / Marcus —

Reviewed the request and the Q2 hiring plan. People Ops + Finance are comfortable approving this hire from the infra pool. A few specifics:

- Recommended level: IC5 (Staff) if candidate has explicit latency/tensor-kernel experience; otherwise IC4 (Senior).
- Comp guidance (US - San Francisco market): base $185,000–$210,000; target total cash + equity (on-target) $240,000–$290,000.
- We can approve an offer up to $300,000 total comp only with explicit director signoff (Markus) and justification; please provide candidate comparisons if you expect to hit that ceiling.
- Headcount: we will convert one infra pool slot (Q2) to a filled req for your team; this counts against the platform hiring plan.

Attached: salary_grid_2026.xlsx for precise banding. For offers, People Ops prefers we make an initial ask at the band midpoint and leave room for negotiation. If Marcus and Markus confirm level and exact offer number, I can generate an offer letter and equity template.

Logging approval: People Ops approves the headcount conversion and the comp band limits above. Please obtain Markus' final signoff if you plan to exceed $290k total comp.

Laura Bennett
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: salary_grid_2026.xlsx",
    "From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@talentbridge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Offer instructions — Carlos Santos (Runtime candidate)

Sarah —

We'd like TalentBridge to extend an offer to Carlos Santos (intro from your team). Below are the specifics to include in the initial offer package:

- Role: Staff Runtime / Inference Infrastructure Engineer (IC5)
- Start: flexible, target 2026-05-01
- Initial offer: base $195,000; target total comp $260,000 (base + equity + expected bonus). This is midpoint-friendly and leaves negotiation room per Laura's guidance.
- Equity: 0.45% RSU vests over 4 years (subject to standard plan language) — include standard equity template.
- Signing bonus: none anticipated unless candidate has competing counteroffer; leave room to add up to $10k discretionary signing bonus pending Markus signoff.
- Contingencies: standard background and reference checks.

Please use the attached offer_template.pdf and JD_runtime_infra.md when building the package. Copy me on the outbound offer email. If salary negotiations exceed $290k total comp, pause and loop in Laura and Markus for final signoff.

Thanks — please confirm ETA to send offer.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Forwarded message: see thread above.

Attachments: offer_template.pdf, JD_runtime_infra.md"

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\",\n  \"space\": \"architecture-and-standards\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Diego Martinez\",\n    \"Sara Kim\",\n    \"Liam O'Connor\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"adr\",\n    \"contract-testing\",\n    \"schema-fencing\",\n    \"ci-cd\",\n    \"conformance\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025\",\n    \"/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"content\": \"Summary\\n\\nThis ADR defines a company-wide standard for declarative contract tests and a complementary \\\"schema fencing\\\" discipline to prevent schema drift between services and the Redwood platform (APIs, telemetry, and model-serving payloads). The goal is to make API and model I/O contracts machine-testable, versioned, and CI-gated, minimizing production surprises and simplifying rollback and compatibility reasoning.\\n\\nContext and motivation\\n\\nRecent incidents and near-misses were traced to silent schema changes that allowed malformed or unexpectedly shaped requests/telemetry to flow into the runtime. Ad-hoc unit tests are insufficient for cross-service contract guarantees because:\\n\\n- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).\\n- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).\\n- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.\\n\\nThis ADR proposes:\\n\\n1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.\\n2. A \\\"schema fencing\\\" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.\\n3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.\\n\\nScope\\n\\nApplies to:\\n\\n- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).\\n- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).\\n- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.\\n\\nOut of scope:\\n\\n- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.\\n- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.\\n\\nKey concepts\\n\\nDeclarative contract test spec (DCTS):\\n- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).\\n- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).\\n\\nSchema fencing:\\n- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.\\n- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.\\n\\nConformance matrix and ledger:\\n- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.\\n- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.\\n\\nRules and compatibility classes\\n\\nFields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:\\n\\n- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.\\n- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.\\n- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.\\n- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).\\n\\nChange proposal workflow (brief)\\n\\n1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.\\n2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.\\n3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.\\n4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.\\n\\nExample DCTS snippet (YAML)\\n\\n# Example: /v1/generate request/response\\n# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml\\n---\\nendpoint: POST /v1/generate\\nscope: public\\nversion: 1.0.0\\nmode: strict\\nrequest: \\n  content-type: application/json\\n  schema: |\\n    type: object\\n    properties:\\n      prompt:\\n        type: string\\n      features:\\n        type: object\\n        additionalProperties: true\\n    required: [prompt]\\nexamples:\\n  - name: simplest\\n    request: {\\\"prompt\\\": \\\"Summarize the following text...\\\"}\\nresponse:\\n  schema: |\\n    type: object\\n    properties:\\n      id: {type: string}\\n      output: {type: string}\\n      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}\\n    required: [id, output]\\npredicates:\\n  - description: output must be non-empty\\n    jq: \\\".output | length > 0\\\"\\nconformance_category: strict\\n\\nAutomation and CI integration\\n\\nCI responsibilities (service repo):\\n- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).\\n- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).\\n- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.\\n\\nCross-repo conformance job (central):\\n- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.\\n- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.\\n\\nConformance ledger and dashboard\\n\\nThe ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)\\n\\nRequired columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.\\n\\nOperational SLOs and alerting\\n\\n- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.\\n- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.\\n\\nGating and release policy\\n\\n- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.\\n- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.\\n\\nRollout and rollback playbook (high level)\\n\\n1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.\\n2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.\\n3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.\\n4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.\\n5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.\\n\\nTelemetry and observability requirements\\n\\nEach contract-test run must emit:\\n- conftest.run_id (UUID)\\n- conftest.service (service name/version)\\n- conftest.endpoint\\n- conftest.test_case_id\\n- conftest.result (pass|fail)\\n- conftest.duration_ms\\n\\nThese fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.\\n\\nOwner and stewardship\\n\\n- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.\\n- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.\\n\\nOpen questions and tradeoffs\\n\\n- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.\\n- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).\\n\\nMigration plan\\n\\n1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.\\n2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.\\n3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.\\n\\nAppendix: sample CLI commands and linter config\\n\\n# Local validation\\n#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml\\n\\n# Publish artifact (CI step)\\n#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml\\n\\n# Central conformance run (dry-run example)\\n#   conformance-runner --matrix-file=matrix.json --artifacts-dir=artifacts/ --output=ledger.csv\\n\\n# Linter rules (excerpt)\\n# required: [owner, risk_level, conformance_category, test_coverage_min]\\n\\nNotes on documentation style\\n\\n- Keep DCTS files short and example-driven. Prefer real-world examples over exhaustive machine-generated schemas.\\n- Use the CP description field to capture rationale and expected client impact.\\n\\nReferences\\n\\n- See canonical request schema and validation playbook: /architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025\\n- Variant compatibility ledger: /architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026\\n\\nApproval\\n\\nApproved by: API Platform leadership, SRE management, and Product for runtime conformance.\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_04b24bf957c047f4b7d8ceefdfde8290\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-declarative-contract-tests-and-schema-fencing-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: architecture-and-standards\n\n:\n\n- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).\n- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).\n- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.\n\nThis ADR proposes:\n\n1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.\n2. A \"schema fencing\" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.\n3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.\n\nScope\n\nApplies to:\n\n- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).\n- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).\n- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.\n\nOut of scope:\n\n- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.\n- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.\n\nKey concepts\n\nDeclarative contract test spec (DCTS):\n- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).\n- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).\n\nSchema fencing:\n- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.\n- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.\n\nConformance matrix and ledger:\n- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.\n- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.\n\nRules and compatibility classes\n\nFields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-declarative-contract-tests-and-schema-fencing-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: architecture-and-standards\n\n- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.\n- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.\n\nRules and compatibility classes\n\nFields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:\n\n- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.\n- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.\n- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.\n- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).\n\nChange proposal workflow (brief)\n\n1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.\n2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.\n3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.\n4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.\n\nExample DCTS snippet (YAML)",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-declarative-contract-tests-and-schema-fencing-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: architecture-and-standards\n\nsnapshot.\n3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.\n4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.\n\nExample DCTS snippet (YAML)\n\n# Example: /v1/generate request/response\n# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml\n---\nendpoint: POST /v1/generate\nscope: public\nversion: 1.0.0\nmode: strict\nrequest: \n  content-type: application/json\n  schema: |\n    type: object\n    properties:\n      prompt:\n        type: string\n      features:\n        type: object\n        additionalProperties: true\n    required: [prompt]\nexamples:\n  - name: simplest\n    request: {\"prompt\": \"Summarize the following text...\"}\nresponse:\n  schema: |\n    type: object\n    properties:\n      id: {type: string}\n      output: {type: string}\n      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}\n    required: [id, output]\npredicates:\n  - description: output must be non-empty\n    jq: \".output | length > 0\"\nconformance_category: strict\n\nAutomation and CI integration\n\nCI responsibilities (service repo):\n- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).\n- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).\n- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.\n\nCross-repo conformance job (central):\n- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.\n- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.\n\nConformance ledger and dashboard",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-declarative-contract-tests-and-schema-fencing-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: architecture-and-standards\n\non successful merge.\n\nCross-repo conformance job (central):\n- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.\n- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.\n\nConformance ledger and dashboard\n\nThe ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)\n\nRequired columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.\n\nOperational SLOs and alerting\n\n- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.\n- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.\n\nGating and release policy\n\n- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.\n- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.\n\nRollout and rollback playbook (high level)\n\n1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.\n2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.\n3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.\n4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.\n5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.\n\nTelemetry and observability requirements",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-declarative-contract-tests-and-schema-fencing-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: architecture-and-standards\n\n: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.\n4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.\n5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.\n\nTelemetry and observability requirements\n\nEach contract-test run must emit:\n- conftest.run_id (UUID)\n- conftest.service (service name/version)\n- conftest.endpoint\n- conftest.test_case_id\n- conftest.result (pass|fail)\n- conftest.duration_ms\n\nThese fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.\n\nOwner and stewardship\n\n- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.\n- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.\n\nOpen questions and tradeoffs\n\n- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.\n- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).\n\nMigration plan\n\n1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.\n2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.\n3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.\n\nAppendix: sample CLI commands and linter config\n\n# Local validation\n#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml\n\n# Publish artifact (CI step)\n#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml",

document.content:
{
  "title": "ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing",
  "space": "architecture-and-standards",
  "author": "Aisha Patel",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-15",
  "last_updated": "2026-03-01",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Martinez",
    "Sara Kim",
    "Liam O'Connor"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "adr",
    "contract-testing",
    "schema-fencing",
    "ci-cd",
    "conformance"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025",
    "/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "Summary

This ADR defines a company-wide standard for declarative contract tests and a complementary "schema fencing" discipline to prevent schema drift between services and the Redwood platform (APIs, telemetry, and model-serving payloads). The goal is to make API and model I/O contracts machine-testable, versioned, and CI-gated, minimizing production surprises and simplifying rollback and compatibility reasoning.

Context and motivation

Recent incidents and near-misses were traced to silent schema changes that allowed malformed or unexpectedly shaped requests/telemetry to flow into the runtime. Ad-hoc unit tests are insufficient for cross-service contract guarantees because:

- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).
- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).
- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.

This ADR proposes:

1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.
2. A "schema fencing" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.
3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.

Scope

Applies to:

- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).
- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).
- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.

Out of scope:

- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.
- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.

Key concepts

Declarative contract test spec (DCTS):
- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).
- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).

Schema fencing:
- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.
- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.

Conformance matrix and ledger:
- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.
- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.

Rules and compatibility classes

Fields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:

- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.
- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.
- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.
- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).

Change proposal workflow (brief)

1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.
2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.
3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.
4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.

Example DCTS snippet (YAML)

# Example: /v1/generate request/response
# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml
---
endpoint: POST /v1/generate
scope: public
version: 1.0.0
mode: strict
request: 
  content-type: application/json
  schema: |
    type: object
    properties:
      prompt:
        type: string
      features:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: true
    required: [prompt]
examples:
  - name: simplest
    request: {"prompt": "Summarize the following text..."}
response:
  schema: |
    type: object
    properties:
      id: {type: string}
      output: {type: string}
      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}
    required: [id, output]
predicates:
  - description: output must be non-empty
    jq: ".output | length > 0"
conformance_category: strict

Automation and CI integration

CI responsibilities (service repo):
- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).
- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).
- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.

Cross-repo conformance job (central):
- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.
- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.

Conformance ledger and dashboard

The ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)

Required columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.

Operational SLOs and alerting

- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.
- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.

Gating and release policy

- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.
- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.

Rollout and rollback playbook (high level)

1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.
2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.
3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.
4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.
5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.

Telemetry and observability requirements

Each contract-test run must emit:
- conftest.run_id (UUID)
- conftest.service (service name/version)
- conftest.endpoint
- conftest.test_case_id
- conftest.result (pass|fail)
- conftest.duration_ms

These fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.

Owner and stewardship

- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.
- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.

Open questions and tradeoffs

- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.
- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).

Migration plan

1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.
2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.
3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.

Appendix: sample CLI commands and linter config

# Local validation
#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml

# Publish artifact (CI step)
#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml

# Central conformance run (dry-run example)
#   conformance-runner --matrix-file=matrix.json --artifacts-dir=artifacts/ --output=ledger.csv

# Linter rules (excerpt)
# required: [owner, risk_level, conformance_category, test_coverage_min]

Notes on documentation style

- Keep DCTS files short and example-driven. Prefer real-world examples over exhaustive machine-generated schemas.
- Use the CP description field to capture rationale and expected client impact.

References

- See canonical request schema and validation playbook: /architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025
- Variant compatibility ledger: /architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026

Approval

Approved by: API Platform leadership, SRE management, and Product for runtime conformance.

2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.
3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.
4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.

CI responsibilities (service repo):
- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).
- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).

Conformance ledger and dashboard

The ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)

Required columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.

Operational SLOs and alerting

- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.
- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.

Gating and release policy

- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.
- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.

Rollout and rollback playbook (high level)

1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.
2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.
3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.
4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.
5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.

Telemetry and observability requirements

Each contract-test run must emit:
- conftest.run_id (UUID)
- conftest.service (service name/version)

These fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.

Owner and stewardship

- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.
- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.

Open questions and tradeoffs

- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.
- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).

Migration plan

1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.
2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.
3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Low-cost config risk calibration and evaluation plan\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/optimize/low-cost-config-risk-calibration-notes.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: product-optimize\n\nk-70b-4bit, smaller context, or smaller model).\n- We care about both aggregate quality deltas and tail/regression slices (sensitive intents).\n- Unit cost is computed from infra cost-per-GPU-hour + observed tokens/sec; we use normalized cost-per-1k-tokens for comparability.\n\nHigh-level proposal:\n1) Standard spreadsheet that computes per-config economics and quality delta per slice.\n2) A two-tier gate: (A) quick automated gate for rollout eligibility based on coarse sampling; (B) deeper gate for scaling beyond canary based on stratified evals and slice-level criteria.\n3) Conservative defaults for pass/fail; teams can propose relaxed thresholds with compensating mitigations (shorter rollout, increased monitoring, immediate fallback).\n\nSpreadsheet layout (columns) — canonical representation for each config tested:\n- config_id\n- model_family\n- variant_notes (quant, batch, ctx_len)\n- measured_p50_latency_ms\n- measured_p95_latency_ms\n- avg_tokens_per_request\n- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd\n- cost_per_request_usd (derived = avg_tokens/1k * cost_per_1k)\n- baseline_quality_score (macro metric e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim or composite eval score)\n- candidate_quality_score\n- delta_quality_vs_baseline (candidate - baseline)\n- relative_cost_savings_pct (1 - candidate_cost / baseline_cost)\n- regression_slices_failed_count\n- total_slices_evaluated\n- slice_fail_rate (regression_slices_failed_count / total_slices_evaluated)\n- recommended_action (auto-pass | canary-only | blocked)\n- notes\n\nKey formulas and examples:\n- cost_per_request_usd = avg_tokens_per_request / 1000 * cost_per_1k_tokens_usd\n- relative_cost_savings_pct = (baseline_cost_per_request - candidate_cost_per_request) / baseline_cost_per_request * 100\n- delta_quality_vs_baseline = candidate_quality_score - baseline_quality_score (positive = better)",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Low-cost config risk calibration and evaluation plan\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/optimize/low-cost-config-risk-calibration-notes.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: product-optimize\n\n- Overall slice_fail_rate must be <= 3% across the canonical slice set (see SLICES below).\n- Relative_cost_savings_pct must be >= 10% to justify complexity.\n- If any single high-sensitivity slice (legal/medical/semantic-constraint) fails > 1% -> auto-block.\n\nDeeper gate (post-canary, before broad rollout):\n- Stratified sample size: 2k examples, weighted by traffic share and slice importance.\n- delta_quality_vs_baseline >= -0.01 (stricter)\n- No slice with delta_quality_vs_baseline < -0.03 (i.e., no catastrophic drop in any slice).\n- Observed p95 latency degradation vs baseline <= +20%.\n- Error rates (generation failures, crashes, low-confidence signals) must be <= baseline + 0.5pp.\n\nSLICES (canonical set to evaluate):\n- short prompt completion (<= 32 tokens)\n- long context summarization (> 512 tokens)\n- instruction-following (2–4 step tasks)\n- dialogue-continuity (multi-turn > 3 turns)\n- code-synthesis (syntactic correctness sample)\n- safety/abusive-content detection (false-positive/false-negative checks)\n- regulatory-sensitive (PII redaction, legal phrasing)\n\nDecision matrix (simplified):\n- Pass quick gate and deep gate -> broad rollout with staged traffic ramp.\n- Pass quick gate, fail deep gate -> extended canary + targeted augment evals OR rollback to baseline for that tenant.\n- Fail quick gate -> do not canary; investigate quantization/kv-cache adjustments.\n\nSampling and statistical notes:\n- Use bootstrapped CIs for delta_quality_vs_baseline; require 95% CI lower bound > -0.03 for quick gate (i.e., we need to be 95% confident candidate is not worse than -3%).\n- For slices with low event frequency, use oversampling and reweighting when computing global metrics.\n- Report both absolute and relative metrics (e.g., absolute BLEU drop and percentile rank change).",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Low-cost config risk calibration and evaluation plan\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/optimize/low-cost-config-risk-calibration-notes.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: product-optimize\n\nfor quick gate (i.e., we need to be 95% confident candidate is not worse than -3%).\n- For slices with low event frequency, use oversampling and reweighting when computing global metrics.\n- Report both absolute and relative metrics (e.g., absolute BLEU drop and percentile rank change).\n\nRollout playbook (practical steps):\n1) Generate candidate config and collect bench numbers in lab (latency, token throughput, memory footprint).\n2) Run automated quick gate against 500-sample scrubbed historical queries. Populate spreadsheet.\n3) If quick gate passes, create canary build (0.5–2% traffic) with aggressive monitoring (per-slice evals, trace sampling).\n4) After 48–72h with canary, run stratified eval (2k+ samples) and compute deeper gate metrics.\n5) If deep gate passes, ramp to 20% then 100% with step checks; if fails at any stage, immediately fallback route to baseline variant.\n\nFallback and mitigation options:\n- Immediate fallback to pinned baseline for affected tenant/route.\n- Reduce context length or batch parameters if regression localized to long-context slices.\n- Use hybrid routing: route safety/regulatory-sensitive requests to baseline while sending rest to candidate.\n\nMonitoring knobs and dashboards to add:\n- Per-config composite quality score time series (hourly)\n- Per-slice fail rates and delta_quality heatmap\n- Cost-per-1k-tokens by config and region\n- Canary vs baseline error traces and generation confidence distributions\n\nOpen questions and tradeoffs (for discussion):\n- How to weight slices in composite score? (equal weights vs traffic-weighted vs business-impact-weighted)\n- When is a 10% cost saving not worth 1% quality loss? propose a default monetary conversion: $ per basis point drop in composite score computed from customer support/retention models (TBD).\n- How to handle model-family drift when baseline changes frequently? suggest automating periodic recalibration windows.",

document.title: Low-cost config risk calibration and evaluation plan
document.content:
{
  "title": "Low-cost config risk calibration and evaluation plan",
  "owner": "Aisha Patel",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/product/optimize/low-cost-config-risk-calibration-notes.json",
  "doc_type": "doc",
  "created_at": "2026-02-10",
  "last_modified": "2026-03-12",
  "collaborators": [
    "Marco Liu",
    "Sofia Reyes",
    "Ben Carter"
  ],
  "team": "product-optimize",
  "status": "in_review",
  "tags": [
    "cost-model",
    "evaluation",
    "quality-gates",
    "low-cost-variants",
    "rollout"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "confluence:OPT-783-low-cost-config-playbook",
    "jira:INF-2314",
    "github:github.com/redwood/infra/pull/497"
  ],
  "content": "Purpose and context:

This note captures an actionable eval plan and spreadsheet layout to calibrate quality gates for lower-cost serving configurations (quantized/fast variants, smaller context, aggressive batching). Goal is to produce deterministic, reviewable gate thresholds that limit regressions while enabling ~15–40% unit-cost savings where appropriate. This document is intentionally pragmatic — lightweight sampling + conservative pass criteria to avoid customer-visible regressions.

Audience:
- Product-optimize owners
- Applied ML + Eval team
- Serving-runtime and Release engineers responsible for rollouts

Assumptions and constraints:
- Baseline = current default production variant for a given model (e.g., rwk-70b-fp16).
- Candidate = low-cost variant (e.g., rwk-70b-4bit, smaller context, or smaller model).
- We care about both aggregate quality deltas and tail/regression slices (sensitive intents).
- Unit cost is computed from infra cost-per-GPU-hour + observed tokens/sec; we use normalized cost-per-1k-tokens for comparability.

High-level proposal:
1) Standard spreadsheet that computes per-config economics and quality delta per slice.
2) A two-tier gate: (A) quick automated gate for rollout eligibility based on coarse sampling; (B) deeper gate for scaling beyond canary based on stratified evals and slice-level criteria.
3) Conservative defaults for pass/fail; teams can propose relaxed thresholds with compensating mitigations (shorter rollout, increased monitoring, immediate fallback).

Spreadsheet layout (columns) — canonical representation for each config tested:
- config_id
- model_family
- variant_notes (quant, batch, ctx_len)
- measured_p50_latency_ms
- measured_p95_latency_ms
- avg_tokens_per_request
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
- cost_per_request_usd (derived = avg_tokens/1k * cost_per_1k)
- baseline_quality_score (macro metric e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim or composite eval score)
- candidate_quality_score
- delta_quality_vs_baseline (candidate - baseline)
- relative_cost_savings_pct (1 - candidate_cost / baseline_cost)
- regression_slices_failed_count
- total_slices_evaluated
- slice_fail_rate (regression_slices_failed_count / total_slices_evaluated)
- recommended_action (auto-pass | canary-only | blocked)
- notes

Key formulas and examples:
- cost_per_request_usd = avg_tokens_per_request / 1000 * cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
- relative_cost_savings_pct = (baseline_cost_per_request - candidate_cost_per_request) / baseline_cost_per_request * 100
- delta_quality_vs_baseline = candidate_quality_score - baseline_quality_score (positive = better)

Sample row (illustrative):
- config_id: low-q4-ctx2-1
- model_family: rwk-70b
- variant_notes: 4-bit, ctx=2k, batch=auto
- measured_p50_latency_ms: 120
- measured_p95_latency_ms: 350
- avg_tokens_per_request: 250
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: 0.0034
- cost_per_request_usd: 0.00085
- baseline_quality_score: 0.812
- candidate_quality_score: 0.793
- delta_quality_vs_baseline: -0.019
- relative_cost_savings_pct: 22.4%
- regression_slices_failed_count: 6
- total_slices_evaluated: 120
- slice_fail_rate: 5.0%
- recommended_action: canary-only
- notes: acceptable for low-risk features; fails on dialogue-continuity slice

Gate definitions (conservative defaults):
Automated quick gate (pre-canary):
- Minimum sample size: 500 examples sampled uniformly from production logs (de-identified).
- Aggregate quality delta must be >= -0.015 (i.e., candidate not worse by more than 1.5 percentage points on composite score).
- Overall slice_fail_rate must be <= 3% across the canonical slice set (see SLICES below).
- Relative_cost_savings_pct must be >= 10% to justify complexity.
- If any single high-sensitivity slice (legal/medical/semantic-constraint) fails > 1% -> auto-block.

Deeper gate (post-canary, before broad rollout):
- Stratified sample size: 2k examples, weighted by traffic share and slice importance.
- delta_quality_vs_baseline >= -0.01 (stricter)
- No slice with delta_quality_vs_baseline < -0.03 (i.e., no catastrophic drop in any slice).
- Observed p95 latency degradation vs baseline <= +20%.
- Error rates (generation failures, crashes, low-confidence signals) must be <= baseline + 0.5pp.

SLICES (canonical set to evaluate):
- short prompt completion (<= 32 tokens)
- long context summarization (> 512 tokens)
- instruction-following (2–4 step tasks)
- dialogue-continuity (multi-turn > 3 turns)
- code-synthesis (syntactic correctness sample)
- safety/abusive-content detection (false-positive/false-negative checks)
- regulatory-sensitive (PII redaction, legal phrasing)

Decision matrix (simplified):
- Pass quick gate and deep gate -> broad rollout with staged traffic ramp.
- Pass quick gate, fail deep gate -> extended canary + targeted augment evals OR rollback to baseline for that tenant.
- Fail quick gate -> do not canary; investigate quantization/kv-cache adjustments.

Sampling and statistical notes:
- Use bootstrapped CIs for delta_quality_vs_baseline; require 95% CI lower bound > -0.03 for quick gate (i.e., we need to be 95% confident candidate is not worse than -3%).
- For slices with low event frequency, use oversampling and reweighting when computing global metrics.
- Report both absolute and relative metrics (e.g., absolute BLEU drop and percentile rank change).

Rollout playbook (practical steps):
1) Generate candidate config and collect bench numbers in lab (latency, token throughput, memory footprint).
2) Run automated quick gate against 500-sample scrubbed historical queries. Populate spreadsheet.
3) If quick gate passes, create canary build (0.5–2% traffic) with aggressive monitoring (per-slice evals, trace sampling).
4) After 48–72h with canary, run stratified eval (2k+ samples) and compute deeper gate metrics.
5) If deep gate passes, ramp to 20% then 100% with step checks; if fails at any stage, immediately fallback route to baseline variant.

Fallback and mitigation options:
- Immediate fallback to pinned baseline for affected tenant/route.
- Reduce context length or batch parameters if regression localized to long-context slices.
- Use hybrid routing: route safety/regulatory-sensitive requests to baseline while sending rest to candidate.

Monitoring knobs and dashboards to add:
- Per-config composite quality score time series (hourly)
- Per-slice fail rates and delta_quality heatmap
- Cost-per-1k-tokens by config and region
- Canary vs baseline error traces and generation confidence distributions

Open questions and tradeoffs (for discussion):
- How to weight slices in composite score? (equal weights vs traffic-weighted vs business-impact-weighted)
- When is a 10% cost saving not worth 1% quality loss? propose a default monetary conversion: $ per basis point drop in composite score computed from customer support/retention models (TBD).
- How to handle model-family drift when baseline changes frequently? suggest automating periodic recalibration windows.

Next actions (owners):
- Aisha: finalize the spreadsheet template and centralize canonical slice list (due 2026-03-05).
- Marco: implement quick-gate script to run on historical logs and output CSV matching layout (WIP, PR linked).
- Sofia: prototype dashboard panels for per-slice pass/fail and cost vs quality scatter.
- Ben: draft tenant-level routing playbook for hybrid strategies.

Appendix — minimal evaluation checklist (to attach to PR/Canary):
- [ ] CSV exported with all spreadsheet columns populated
- [ ] 500-sample quick-gate raw outputs and bootstrap CI report
- [ ] Canary telemetry enabled and alerting thresholds configured
- [ ] Rollback policy specified and tested in staging
- [ ] Linked PR and Confluence playbook referenced

End of note.

Contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) for questions or to request clarification on the defaults.

This note captures an actionable eval plan and spreadsheet layout to calibrate quality gates for lower-cost serving configurations (quantized/fast variants, smaller context, aggressive batching).     "id": "dsid_184be937d34a412ab5e61366d54d8ed6",

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/google_drive",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\",\n  \"owner\": \"Jordan Lee\",\n  \"drive_area\": \"shared_drives\",\n  \"path\": \"shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\",\n  \"doc_type\": \"doc\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-07\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2026-01-12\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Ravi Menon\",\n    \"Miles Thornton\",\n    \"Benji Okafor\",\n    \"Mina Haddad\",\n    \"Ethan Park\",\n    \"Allison Grant\"\n  ],\n  \"team\": \"eng-platform\",\n  \"status\": \"draft\",\n  \"tags\": [\n    \"failover\",\n    \"policy-engine\",\n    \"determinism\",\n    \"routing\",\n    \"guardrails\",\n    \"sre\",\n    \"reliability-program\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_artifacts\": [\n    \"Linear: ENG-2411\",\n    \"Linear: ENG-2412\",\n    \"Linear: ENG-2415\",\n    \"Linear: ENG-2416\",\n    \"Confluence: adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy\",\n    \"Confluence: adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback\",\n    \"GitHub: redwood/pr-19812-policy-engine-signal-priority (planned)\",\n    \"GitHub: redwood/pr-19815-routing-policy-rollback-safety (planned)\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Context / why this exists\\n- We\\u2019re upgrading regional failover automation as part of Reliability Program (Q1\\u2013Q2 2026). Today, routing policy evaluation has a few gaps:\\n  - Non-deterministic behavior in edge cases (e.g., multiple signals firing, partial signal availability, time-window ambiguity).\\n  - Hard to reason about priority across trigger signals (reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity exhaustion).\\n  - No first-class \\u201chold-down\\u201d / dampening in evaluation; logic is split between policy rules and external controller.\\n  - No consistent mechanism to enforce safety constraints per tenant/tier (max flips, blast radius caps, required approval).\\n\\nGoals\\n- Add policy engine primitives so failover decisioning is:\\n  - Deterministic and auditable (same inputs => same decision; explainability built-in).\\n  - Compatible with ADR-042 (signal priority + corroboration) and ADR-043 (rollback + anti-flap).\\n  - Safe by default (rate limits, required corroboration, blast radius constraints).\\n- Support both:\\n  - \\u201cRecommend\\u201d (dry-run) mode: compute candidate flips + evidence.\\n  - \\u201cEnforce\\u201d mode: same evaluation but returns executable actions.\\n\\nNon-goals\\n- Replace the automation controller. The controller still orchestrates execution, approvals, and cross-system workflow.\\n- Re-architect signal ingestion. We consume normalized, time-bucketed signals from Region Health + SLO toolkit.\\n- Build customer-facing UI here.\\n\\nTerminology\\n- Policy: configuration describing routing behavior for a route/service/model/tier.\\n- Region set: primary and fallback regions eligible for this route.\\n- Trigger signal: normalized boolean or scalar indicating regional impairment or risk.\\n- Decision: computed outcome (no-op, failover, partial shift, rollback, hold).\\n- Action: executable change (policy flip, weight adjustment, circuit breaker mode) emitted by controller.\\n\\nInputs / data model assumptions\\n- Policy engine receives inputs as a single evaluation payload, including:\\n  - route_id (e.g., hosted.chat.completions, dedicated.pool.<pool_id>)\\n  - tenant_id (optional for shared Hosted; required for Dedicated)\\n  - tenant_tier (free/pro/enterprise/dedicated)\\n  - current_routing_state (primary region, weights, last_flip_at)\\n  - signals (per region, per signal type):\\n    - reachability: ok|degraded|down + confidence + last_updated\\n    - errors_5xx_burn: burn_rate + window + confidence\\n    - tail_latency_burn: burn_rate + p95/p99 deltas + confidence\\n    - capacity_headroom: percent + \\u201chard gate\\u201d boolean\\n    - control_plane_health (optional): ok|degraded|down\\n  - evaluation_time (UTC epoch + monotonic sequence)\\n  - constraints (policy-level + tenant-level): max_flips_per_hour, min_hold_down_seconds, require_approval, blast_radius_limit\\n\\nDeterminism requirements (core)\\n1) Stable ordering\\n- Evaluation must not depend on map iteration order.\\n- Rule matching must define explicit ordering: by priority, then by tie-breakers.\\n\\n2) Stable time semantics\\n- All windowed signals must be anchored to evaluation_time and include:\\n  - effective_start, effective_end, and a \\u201cfreshness\\u201d timestamp.\\n- Engine must treat stale signals consistently:\\n  - If authoritative signals are stale beyond threshold, decision = HOLD (do not fail over) unless reachability is explicitly DOWN with high confidence.\\n\\n3) Single decision per evaluation\\n- For a given (route_id, tenant_id, evaluation_time), engine emits exactly one decision object, even if multiple actions are possible.\\n- Multi-step actions (e.g., drain -> shift weights -> finalize) must be represented as a sequence recommendation but still within a single decision record.\\n\\n4) Explainability\\n- Decision must include:\\n  - decision_type (NO_OP | FAILOVER | PARTIAL_SHIFT | ROLLBACK | HOLD)\\n  - chosen_reason (canonical enum)\\n  - evidence: ordered list of signals used, with values, freshness, and thresholds.\\n  - rejected_candidates: (optional) top 1\\u20133 alternatives and why they were not selected.\\n\\nProposed changes to policy engine\\nA) New predicates / functions\\n1) region_health(region, signal_type) -> {status, value, confidence, freshness_seconds}\\n- Wrapper that pulls normalized data from payload and enforces freshness calculations.\\n\\n2) is_authoritative_reachability_down(region) -> bool\\n- True only if:\\n  - reachability.status == down\\n  - confidence >= configured_min_confidence (default 0.9)\\n  - freshness_seconds <= reachability_max_staleness (default 30s)\\n\\n3) burn_rate_exceeded(region, metric, window, threshold) -> bool\\n- Works for errors_5xx_burn and tail_latency_burn.\\n- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.\\n\\n4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool\\n- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.\\n- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.\\n\\n5) corroborated(primary_signal, secondary_signal) -> bool\\n- Enforces ADR-042 \\u201crequired corroboration signals\\u201d when configured.\\n- Example: if tail latency burn triggers, require either 5xx burn OR reachability degraded/down OR control plane degraded.\\n\\n6) hold_down_active(last_flip_at, min_hold_down_seconds) -> bool\\n- If true, policy engine returns HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative.\\n\\n7) flip_budget_ok(tenant_id, route_id, max_flips_per_hour) -> bool\\n- Input includes a precomputed counter from controller/state store (policy engine does not store state).\\n\\n8) blast_radius_ok(tenant_tier, requested_action) -> bool\\n- Enforces \\u201ccan\\u2019t shift more than X% traffic for tier Y without approval\\u201d.\\n- For Hosted, blast radius is route-scoped; for Dedicated, pool-scoped.\\n\\nB) Deterministic evaluation mode (required)\\n- Add an \\u201cevaluation_mode\\u201d field:\\n  - recommend: compute decision + evidence; do not mark as executable\\n  - enforce: compute decision; include explicit requested_action(s)\\n- Engine must produce identical decision_type and evidence in both modes (action packaging differs).\\n\\nC) Signal hierarchy evaluation (ADR-042)\\nPriority order (proposed canonical order for v1):\\n1) Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback)\\n2) Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity\\n3) Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained\\n4) Capacity exhaustion / hard gate => HOLD + load shed (controller action), avoid shifting into constrained region\\n5) Control plane degradation => HOLD (do not flip rapidly; prevent oscillation)\\n\\nNotes:\\n- \\u201cNo healthy fallback\\u201d means every eligible fallback region fails capacity_hard_gate OR reachability is down OR stale beyond threshold.\\n- If no healthy fallback, decision should be HOLD and include \\u201cdegrade_allowed=true\\u201d hint (controller can activate load shedding / retry-after).\\n\\nD) Policy language / config schema additions\\nAdd new fields (names tentative):\\n- failover:\\n  - enabled: boolean\\n  - eligible_regions: [us-east, eu-west, ...]\\n  - signal_requirements:\\n    - primary_trigger: enum\\n    - corroboration: [enum]\\n    - min_confidence: float\\n    - max_staleness_seconds: int\\n  - dampening:\\n    - min_hold_down_seconds: int\\n    - require_sustain_seconds: int (for non-reachability triggers)\\n  - safety:\\n    - require_approval: boolean (default true for prod initially)\\n    - max_flips_per_hour: int\\n    - max_traffic_shift_percent: int\\n    - rollback:\\n      - auto_rollback_enabled: boolean\\n      - rollback_after_seconds: int\\n      - rollback_require_healthy_primary_seconds: int\\n\\nE) Output schema\\nDecision output (single object, JSON):\\n- decision_id (stable hash of route_id + tenant_id + evaluation_time + policy_version)\\n- policy_version\\n- evaluation_time\\n- decision_type\\n- chosen_reason\\n- target_state (string encoding; owned by controller)\\n- requested_actions (string encoding; empty in recommend mode)\\n- evidence (string encoding; ordered)\\n- annotations (string encoding; includes thresholds, staleness, hold-down state)\\n\\nNote: In our implementation we\\u2019ll likely use structured objects, but for logging/audit we must generate a stable, versioned string representation.\\n\\nSafety constraints (ADR-043 alignment)\\n- Anti-flap:\\n  - Enforce hold-down between flips for non-reachability triggers.\\n  - Any rollback decision must respect a separate rollback hold-down (avoid ping-pong between primary and fallback).\\n- Rate limiting:\\n  - flip_budget_ok must be true, else HOLD.\\n- Approval hooks:\\n  - If require_approval is true, decision_type can still be FAILOVER but requested_actions must be empty and \\u201capproval_required=true\\u201d annotation set.\\n- Tenant/tier gates:\\n  - Enterprise/Dedicated can be configured with stricter \\u201cdo not cross data residency boundary\\u201d constraint (policy engine should surface \\u201cconstraint_violation:data_residency\\u201d rather than attempt partial shifts).\\n\\nEdge cases and expected behavior\\n1) Partial outage in primary region\\n- Reachability degraded (not down), 5xx burn elevated, capacity OK in fallback.\\n- Expected: PARTIAL_SHIFT (e.g., shift 25\\u201350% depending on max_traffic_shift_percent) if corroborated. If sustained and escalates to reachability down or error burn becomes severe => FAILOVER.\\n\\n2) Signal missing / ingestion delayed\\n- Any authoritative signal is stale beyond max_staleness_seconds.\\n- Expected: HOLD. Evidence must explicitly call out staleness and which signal blocked action.\\n\\n3) Fallback region constrained\\n- Primary is failing (5xx burn), fallback capacity_hard_gate true.\\n- Expected: HOLD + annotate \\u201cfallback_unhealthy_due_to_capacity\\u201d. Controller should invoke load shedding and retry-after rather than shifting load.\\n\\n4) Control plane degraded\\n- Control plane health degraded; data plane signals ambiguous.\\n- Expected: HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative. (Avoid flipping policies when control plane is suspect.)\\n\\n5) Multi-fallback selection\\n- If multiple eligible fallback regions are healthy, selection tie-breakers:\\n  1) policy-specified order\\n  2) lowest latency probe (if available in inputs)\\n  3) highest capacity headroom\\n  4) stable sort by region name\\n\\nTesting plan (draft)\\nUnit tests\\n- Determinism:\\n  - Same payload with randomized key order => same decision_id, decision_type, evidence ordering.\\n- Staleness gating:\\n  - Stale error burn + fresh reachability OK => HOLD.\\n- Priority:\\n  - Reachability DOWN overrides hold-down.\\n  - 5xx burn overrides latency burn when both exceed thresholds.\\n\\nIntegration tests\\n- Replay recorded signal snapshots from staging incidents + controlled game day traces.\\n- Validate output is compatible with controller dry-run UX (must contain reasons + evidence).\\n\\nPerformance considerations\\n- Evaluation must be cheap; do not add per-eval remote calls.\\n- Evidence strings must be bounded in size. Cap rejected_candidates and evidence list.\\n\\nOperational / observability hooks\\n- Emit a single log line per decision with:\\n  - decision_id, route_id, tenant_id (hashed in shared Hosted contexts), decision_type, chosen_reason\\n  - key thresholds and freshness\\n- Export metrics:\\n  - policy_engine_decisions_total{decision_type, chosen_reason, tier}\\n  - policy_engine_hold_reasons_total{reason}\\n  - policy_engine_eval_latency_ms\\n\\nOpen questions\\n- Exact shape of \\u201ctarget_state\\u201d string: should it be a controller-owned serialization of desired weights, or should the policy engine output high-level intent only?\\n- Do we want PARTIAL_SHIFT as a first-class decision type (recommended), or represent it as FAILOVER with weight < 100%?\\n- How strict should corroboration be for tail latency burn? (ADR-042 indicates corroboration required; we need the exact default set.)\\n- Where should data residency constraints live?\\n  - Option A: policy engine validates \\u201cregion set allowed\\u201d and blocks action.\\n  - Option B: upstream policy compilation prevents invalid eligible_regions.\\n\\nNear-term next steps\\n- Align with Miles/Ravi on canonical signal enum + reason enum.\\n- Draft schema PR for policy config additions (behind feature flag).\\n- Implement deterministic ordering + evidence output in policy engine.\\n- Wire to dry-run mode (ENG-2415) so the controller can display \\u201crecommended action + confidence + evidence\\u201d on game day.\\n\\nAppendix: candidate enums (WIP)\\nchosen_reason\\n- REACHABILITY_DOWN\\n- ERROR_BURN_FAST\\n- LATENCY_BURN_SUSTAINED\\n- CAPACITY_HARD_GATE\\n- SIGNALS_STALE\\n- HOLD_DOWN_ACTIVE\\n- FLIP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED\\n- CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION_DATA_RESIDENCY\\n- NO_HEALTHY_FALLBACK\\n\\nsignal_type\\n- REACHABILITY\\n- ERRORS_5XX_BURN\\n- TAIL_LATENCY_BURN\\n- CAPACITY_HEADROOM\\n- CONTROL_PLANE_HEALTH\\n\",\n  \"original_location\": \"google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_184be937d34a412ab5e61366d54d8ed6\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\nreachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity exhaustion).\n  - No first-class “hold-down” / dampening in evaluation; logic is split between policy rules and external controller.\n  - No consistent mechanism to enforce safety constraints per tenant/tier (max flips, blast radius caps, required approval).\n\nGoals\n- Add policy engine primitives so failover decisioning is:\n  - Deterministic and auditable (same inputs => same decision; explainability built-in).\n  - Compatible with ADR-042 (signal priority + corroboration) and ADR-043 (rollback + anti-flap).\n  - Safe by default (rate limits, required corroboration, blast radius constraints).\n- Support both:\n  - “Recommend” (dry-run) mode: compute candidate flips + evidence.\n  - “Enforce” mode: same evaluation but returns executable actions.\n\nNon-goals\n- Replace the automation controller. The controller still orchestrates execution, approvals, and cross-system workflow.\n- Re-architect signal ingestion. We consume normalized, time-bucketed signals from Region Health + SLO toolkit.\n- Build customer-facing UI here.\n\nTerminology\n- Policy: configuration describing routing behavior for a route/service/model/tier.\n- Region set: primary and fallback regions eligible for this route.\n- Trigger signal: normalized boolean or scalar indicating regional impairment or risk.\n- Decision: computed outcome (no-op, failover, partial shift, rollback, hold).\n- Action: executable change (policy flip, weight adjustment, circuit breaker mode) emitted by controller.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\nset: primary and fallback regions eligible for this route.\n- Trigger signal: normalized boolean or scalar indicating regional impairment or risk.\n- Decision: computed outcome (no-op, failover, partial shift, rollback, hold).\n- Action: executable change (policy flip, weight adjustment, circuit breaker mode) emitted by controller.\n\nInputs / data model assumptions\n- Policy engine receives inputs as a single evaluation payload, including:\n  - route_id (e.g., hosted.chat.completions, dedicated.pool.<pool_id>)\n  - tenant_id (optional for shared Hosted; required for Dedicated)\n  - tenant_tier (free/pro/enterprise/dedicated)\n  - current_routing_state (primary region, weights, last_flip_at)\n  - signals (per region, per signal type):\n    - reachability: ok|degraded|down + confidence + last_updated\n    - errors_5xx_burn: burn_rate + window + confidence\n    - tail_latency_burn: burn_rate + p95/p99 deltas + confidence\n    - capacity_headroom: percent + “hard gate” boolean\n    - control_plane_health (optional): ok|degraded|down\n  - evaluation_time (UTC epoch + monotonic sequence)\n  - constraints (policy-level + tenant-level): max_flips_per_hour, min_hold_down_seconds, require_approval, blast_radius_limit\n\nDeterminism requirements (core)\n1) Stable ordering\n- Evaluation must not depend on map iteration order.\n- Rule matching must define explicit ordering: by priority, then by tie-breakers.\n\n2) Stable time semantics\n- All windowed signals must be anchored to evaluation_time and include:\n  - effective_start, effective_end, and a “freshness” timestamp.\n- Engine must treat stale signals consistently:\n  - If authoritative signals are stale beyond threshold, decision = HOLD (do not fail over) unless reachability is explicitly DOWN with high confidence.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\ned signals must be anchored to evaluation_time and include:\n  - effective_start, effective_end, and a “freshness” timestamp.\n- Engine must treat stale signals consistently:\n  - If authoritative signals are stale beyond threshold, decision = HOLD (do not fail over) unless reachability is explicitly DOWN with high confidence.\n\n3) Single decision per evaluation\n- For a given (route_id, tenant_id, evaluation_time), engine emits exactly one decision object, even if multiple actions are possible.\n- Multi-step actions (e.g., drain -> shift weights -> finalize) must be represented as a sequence recommendation but still within a single decision record.\n\n4) Explainability\n- Decision must include:\n  - decision_type (NO_OP | FAILOVER | PARTIAL_SHIFT | ROLLBACK | HOLD)\n  - chosen_reason (canonical enum)\n  - evidence: ordered list of signals used, with values, freshness, and thresholds.\n  - rejected_candidates: (optional) top 1–3 alternatives and why they were not selected.\n\nProposed changes to policy engine\nA) New predicates / functions\n1) region_health(region, signal_type) -> {status, value, confidence, freshness_seconds}\n- Wrapper that pulls normalized data from payload and enforces freshness calculations.\n\n2) is_authoritative_reachability_down(region) -> bool\n- True only if:\n  - reachability.status == down\n  - confidence >= configured_min_confidence (default 0.9)\n  - freshness_seconds <= reachability_max_staleness (default 30s)\n\n3) burn_rate_exceeded(region, metric, window, threshold) -> bool\n- Works for errors_5xx_burn and tail_latency_burn.\n- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.\n\n4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool\n- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.\n- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.",
