{
  "title": "Low-cost config risk calibration and evaluation plan",
  "owner": "Aisha Patel",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/product/optimize/low-cost-config-risk-calibration-notes.json",
  "doc_type": "doc",
  "created_at": "2026-02-10",
  "last_modified": "2026-03-12",
  "collaborators": [
    "Marco Liu",
    "Sofia Reyes",
    "Ben Carter"
  ],
  "team": "product-optimize",
  "status": "in_review",
  "tags": [
    "cost-model",
    "evaluation",
    "quality-gates",
    "low-cost-variants",
    "rollout"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "confluence:OPT-783-low-cost-config-playbook",
    "jira:INF-2314",
    "github:github.com/redwood/infra/pull/497"
  ],
  "content": "Purpose and context:

This note captures an actionable eval plan and spreadsheet layout to calibrate quality gates for lower-cost serving configurations (quantized/fast variants, smaller context, aggressive batching). Goal is to produce deterministic, reviewable gate thresholds that limit regressions while enabling ~15–40% unit-cost savings where appropriate. This document is intentionally pragmatic — lightweight sampling + conservative pass criteria to avoid customer-visible regressions.

Audience:
- Product-optimize owners
- Applied ML + Eval team
- Serving-runtime and Release engineers responsible for rollouts

Assumptions and constraints:
- Baseline = current default production variant for a given model (e.g., rwk-70b-fp16).
- Candidate = low-cost variant (e.g., rwk-70b-4bit, smaller context, or smaller model).
- We care about both aggregate quality deltas and tail/regression slices (sensitive intents).
- Unit cost is computed from infra cost-per-GPU-hour + observed tokens/sec; we use normalized cost-per-1k-tokens for comparability.

High-level proposal:
1) Standard spreadsheet that computes per-config economics and quality delta per slice.
2) A two-tier gate: (A) quick automated gate for rollout eligibility based on coarse sampling; (B) deeper gate for scaling beyond canary based on stratified evals and slice-level criteria.
3) Conservative defaults for pass/fail; teams can propose relaxed thresholds with compensating mitigations (shorter rollout, increased monitoring, immediate fallback).

Spreadsheet layout (columns) — canonical representation for each config tested:
- config_id
- model_family
- variant_notes (quant, batch, ctx_len)
- measured_p50_latency_ms
- measured_p95_latency_ms
- avg_tokens_per_request
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
- cost_per_request_usd (derived = avg_tokens/1k * cost_per_1k)
- baseline_quality_score (macro metric e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim or composite eval score)
- candidate_quality_score
- delta_quality_vs_baseline (candidate - baseline)
- relative_cost_savings_pct (1 - candidate_cost / baseline_cost)
- regression_slices_failed_count
- total_slices_evaluated
- slice_fail_rate (regression_slices_failed_count / total_slices_evaluated)
- recommended_action (auto-pass | canary-only | blocked)
- notes

Key formulas and examples:
- cost_per_request_usd = avg_tokens_per_request / 1000 * cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
- relative_cost_savings_pct = (baseline_cost_per_request - candidate_cost_per_request) / baseline_cost_per_request * 100
- delta_quality_vs_baseline = candidate_quality_score - baseline_quality_score (positive = better)

Sample row (illustrative):
- config_id: low-q4-ctx2-1
- model_family: rwk-70b
- variant_notes: 4-bit, ctx=2k, batch=auto
- measured_p50_latency_ms: 120
- measured_p95_latency_ms: 350
- avg_tokens_per_request: 250
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: 0.0034
- cost_per_request_usd: 0.00085
- baseline_quality_score: 0.812
- candidate_quality_score: 0.793
- delta_quality_vs_baseline: -0.019
- relative_cost_savings_pct: 22.4%
- regression_slices_failed_count: 6
- total_slices_evaluated: 120
- slice_fail_rate: 5.0%
- recommended_action: canary-only
- notes: acceptable for low-risk features; fails on dialogue-continuity slice

Gate definitions (conservative defaults):
Automated quick gate (pre-canary):
- Minimum sample size: 500 examples sampled uniformly from production logs (de-identified).
- Aggregate quality delta must be >= -0.015 (i.e., candidate not worse by more than 1.5 percentage points on composite score).
- Overall slice_fail_rate must be <= 3% across the canonical slice set (see SLICES below).
- Relative_cost_savings_pct must be >= 10% to justify complexity.
- If any single high-sensitivity slice (legal/medical/semantic-constraint) fails > 1% -> auto-block.

Deeper gate (post-canary, before broad rollout):
- Stratified sample size: 2k examples, weighted by traffic share and slice importance.
- delta_quality_vs_baseline >= -0.01 (stricter)
- No slice with delta_quality_vs_baseline < -0.03 (i.e., no catastrophic drop in any slice).
- Observed p95 latency degradation vs baseline <= +20%.
- Error rates (generation failures, crashes, low-confidence signals) must be <= baseline + 0.5pp.

SLICES (canonical set to evaluate):
- short prompt completion (<= 32 tokens)
- long context summarization (> 512 tokens)
- instruction-following (2–4 step tasks)
- dialogue-continuity (multi-turn > 3 turns)
- code-synthesis (syntactic correctness sample)
- safety/abusive-content detection (false-positive/false-negative checks)
- regulatory-sensitive (PII redaction, legal phrasing)

Decision matrix (simplified):
- Pass quick gate and deep gate -> broad rollout with staged traffic ramp.
- Pass quick gate, fail deep gate -> extended canary + targeted augment evals OR rollback to baseline for that tenant.
- Fail quick gate -> do not canary; investigate quantization/kv-cache adjustments.

Sampling and statistical notes:
- Use bootstrapped CIs for delta_quality_vs_baseline; require 95% CI lower bound > -0.03 for quick gate (i.e., we need to be 95% confident candidate is not worse than -3%).
- For slices with low event frequency, use oversampling and reweighting when computing global metrics.
- Report both absolute and relative metrics (e.g., absolute BLEU drop and percentile rank change).

Rollout playbook (practical steps):
1) Generate candidate config and collect bench numbers in lab (latency, token throughput, memory footprint).
2) Run automated quick gate against 500-sample scrubbed historical queries. Populate spreadsheet.
3) If quick gate passes, create canary build (0.5–2% traffic) with aggressive monitoring (per-slice evals, trace sampling).
4) After 48–72h with canary, run stratified eval (2k+ samples) and compute deeper gate metrics.
5) If deep gate passes, ramp to 20% then 100% with step checks; if fails at any stage, immediately fallback route to baseline variant.

Fallback and mitigation options:
- Immediate fallback to pinned baseline for affected tenant/route.
- Reduce context length or batch parameters if regression localized to long-context slices.
- Use hybrid routing: route safety/regulatory-sensitive requests to baseline while sending rest to candidate.

Monitoring knobs and dashboards to add:
- Per-config composite quality score time series (hourly)
- Per-slice fail rates and delta_quality heatmap
- Cost-per-1k-tokens by config and region
- Canary vs baseline error traces and generation confidence distributions

Open questions and tradeoffs (for discussion):
- How to weight slices in composite score? (equal weights vs traffic-weighted vs business-impact-weighted)
- When is a 10% cost saving not worth 1% quality loss? propose a default monetary conversion: $ per basis point drop in composite score computed from customer support/retention models (TBD).
- How to handle model-family drift when baseline changes frequently? suggest automating periodic recalibration windows.

Next actions (owners):
- Aisha: finalize the spreadsheet template and centralize canonical slice list (due 2026-03-05).
- Marco: implement quick-gate script to run on historical logs and output CSV matching layout (WIP, PR linked).
- Sofia: prototype dashboard panels for per-slice pass/fail and cost vs quality scatter.
- Ben: draft tenant-level routing playbook for hybrid strategies.

Appendix — minimal evaluation checklist (to attach to PR/Canary):
- [ ] CSV exported with all spreadsheet columns populated
- [ ] 500-sample quick-gate raw outputs and bootstrap CI report
- [ ] Canary telemetry enabled and alerting thresholds configured
- [ ] Rollback policy specified and tested in staging
- [ ] Linked PR and Confluence playbook referenced

End of note.

Contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) for questions or to request clarification on the defaults.

    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\",\n  \"owner\": \"Jordan Lee\",\n  \"drive_area\": \"shared_drives\",\n  \"path\": \"shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\",\n  \"doc_type\": \"doc\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-07\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2026-01-12\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Ravi Menon\",\n    \"Miles Thornton\",\n    \"Benji Okafor\",\n    \"Mina Haddad\",\n    \"Ethan Park\",\n    \"Allison Grant\"\n  ],\n  \"team\": \"eng-platform\",\n  \"status\": \"draft\",\n  \"tags\": [\n    \"failover\",\n    \"policy-engine\",\n    \"determinism\",\n    \"routing\",\n    \"guardrails\",\n    \"sre\",\n    \"reliability-program\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_artifacts\": [\n    \"Linear: ENG-2411\",\n    \"Linear: ENG-2412\",\n    \"Linear: ENG-2415\",\n    \"Linear: ENG-2416\",\n    \"Confluence: adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy\",\n    \"Confluence: adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback\",\n    \"GitHub: redwood/pr-19812-policy-engine-signal-priority (planned)\",\n    \"GitHub: redwood/pr-19815-routing-policy-rollback-safety (planned)\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Context / why this exists\\n- We\\u2019re upgrading regional failover automation as part of Reliability Program (Q1\\u2013Q2 2026). Today, routing policy evaluation has a few gaps:\\n  - Non-deterministic behavior in edge cases (e.g., multiple signals firing, partial signal availability, time-window ambiguity).\\n  - Hard to reason about priority across trigger signals (reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity exhaustion).\\n  - No first-class \\u201chold-down\\u201d / dampening in evaluation; logic is split between policy rules and external controller.\\n  - No consistent mechanism to enforce safety constraints per tenant/tier (max flips, blast radius caps, required approval).\\n\\nGoals\\n- Add policy engine primitives so failover decisioning is:\\n  - Deterministic and auditable (same inputs => same decision; explainability built-in).\\n  - Compatible with ADR-042 (signal priority + corroboration) and ADR-043 (rollback + anti-flap).\\n  - Safe by default (rate limits, required corroboration, blast radius constraints).\\n- Support both:\\n  - \\u201cRecommend\\u201d (dry-run) mode: compute candidate flips + evidence.\\n  - \\u201cEnforce\\u201d mode: same evaluation but returns executable actions.\\n\\nNon-goals\\n- Replace the automation controller. The controller still orchestrates execution, approvals, and cross-system workflow.\\n- Re-architect signal ingestion. We consume normalized, time-bucketed signals from Region Health + SLO toolkit.\\n- Build customer-facing UI here.\\n\\nTerminology\\n- Policy: configuration describing routing behavior for a route/service/model/tier.\\n- Region set: primary and fallback regions eligible for this route.\\n- Trigger signal: normalized boolean or scalar indicating regional impairment or risk.\\n- Decision: computed outcome (no-op, failover, partial shift, rollback, hold).\\n- Action: executable change (policy flip, weight adjustment, circuit breaker mode) emitted by controller.\\n\\nInputs / data model assumptions\\n- Policy engine receives inputs as a single evaluation payload, including:\\n  - route_id (e.g., hosted.chat.completions, dedicated.pool.<pool_id>)\\n  - tenant_id (optional for shared Hosted; required for Dedicated)\\n  - tenant_tier (free/pro/enterprise/dedicated)\\n  - current_routing_state (primary region, weights, last_flip_at)\\n  - signals (per region, per signal type):\\n    - reachability: ok|degraded|down + confidence + last_updated\\n    - errors_5xx_burn: burn_rate + window + confidence\\n    - tail_latency_burn: burn_rate + p95/p99 deltas + confidence\\n    - capacity_headroom: percent + \\u201chard gate\\u201d boolean\\n    - control_plane_health (optional): ok|degraded|down\\n  - evaluation_time (UTC epoch + monotonic sequence)\\n  - constraints (policy-level + tenant-level): max_flips_per_hour, min_hold_down_seconds, require_approval, blast_radius_limit\\n\\nDeterminism requirements (core)\\n1) Stable ordering\\n- Evaluation must not depend on map iteration order.\\n- Rule matching must define explicit ordering: by priority, then by tie-breakers.\\n\\n2) Stable time semantics\\n- All windowed signals must be anchored to evaluation_time and include:\\n  - effective_start, effective_end, and a \\u201cfreshness\\u201d timestamp.\\n- Engine must treat stale signals consistently:\\n  - If authoritative signals are stale beyond threshold, decision = HOLD (do not fail over) unless reachability is explicitly DOWN with high confidence.\\n\\n3) Single decision per evaluation\\n- For a given (route_id, tenant_id, evaluation_time), engine emits exactly one decision object, even if multiple actions are possible.\\n- Multi-step actions (e.g., drain -> shift weights -> finalize) must be represented as a sequence recommendation but still within a single decision record.\\n\\n4) Explainability\\n- Decision must include:\\n  - decision_type (NO_OP | FAILOVER | PARTIAL_SHIFT | ROLLBACK | HOLD)\\n  - chosen_reason (canonical enum)\\n  - evidence: ordered list of signals used, with values, freshness, and thresholds.\\n  - rejected_candidates: (optional) top 1\\u20133 alternatives and why they were not selected.\\n\\nProposed changes to policy engine\\nA) New predicates / functions\\n1) region_health(region, signal_type) -> {status, value, confidence, freshness_seconds}\\n- Wrapper that pulls normalized data from payload and enforces freshness calculations.\\n\\n2) is_authoritative_reachability_down(region) -> bool\\n- True only if:\\n  - reachability.status == down\\n  - confidence >= configured_min_confidence (default 0.9)\\n  - freshness_seconds <= reachability_max_staleness (default 30s)\\n\\n3) burn_rate_exceeded(region, metric, window, threshold) -> bool\\n- Works for errors_5xx_burn and tail_latency_burn.\\n- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.\\n\\n4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool\\n- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.\\n- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.\\n\\n5) corroborated(primary_signal, secondary_signal) -> bool\\n- Enforces ADR-042 \\u201crequired corroboration signals\\u201d when configured.\\n- Example: if tail latency burn triggers, require either 5xx burn OR reachability degraded/down OR control plane degraded.\\n\\n6) hold_down_active(last_flip_at, min_hold_down_seconds) -> bool\\n- If true, policy engine returns HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative.\\n\\n7) flip_budget_ok(tenant_id, route_id, max_flips_per_hour) -> bool\\n- Input includes a precomputed counter from controller/state store (policy engine does not store state).\\n\\n8) blast_radius_ok(tenant_tier, requested_action) -> bool\\n- Enforces \\u201ccan\\u2019t shift more than X% traffic for tier Y without approval\\u201d.\\n- For Hosted, blast radius is route-scoped; for Dedicated, pool-scoped.\\n\\nB) Deterministic evaluation mode (required)\\n- Add an \\u201cevaluation_mode\\u201d field:\\n  - recommend: compute decision + evidence; do not mark as executable\\n  - enforce: compute decision; include explicit requested_action(s)\\n- Engine must produce identical decision_type and evidence in both modes (action packaging differs).\\n\\nC) Signal hierarchy evaluation (ADR-042)\\nPriority order (proposed canonical order for v1):\\n1) Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback)\\n2) Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity\\n3) Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained\\n4) Capacity exhaustion / hard gate => HOLD + load shed (controller action), avoid shifting into constrained region\\n5) Control plane degradation => HOLD (do not flip rapidly; prevent oscillation)\\n\\nNotes:\\n- \\u201cNo healthy fallback\\u201d means every eligible fallback region fails capacity_hard_gate OR reachability is down OR stale beyond threshold.\\n- If no healthy fallback, decision should be HOLD and include \\u201cdegrade_allowed=true\\u201d hint (controller can activate load shedding / retry-after).\\n\\nD) Policy language / config schema additions\\nAdd new fields (names tentative):\\n- failover:\\n  - enabled: boolean\\n  - eligible_regions: [us-east, eu-west, ...]\\n  - signal_requirements:\\n    - primary_trigger: enum\\n    - corroboration: [enum]\\n    - min_confidence: float\\n    - max_staleness_seconds: int\\n  - dampening:\\n    - min_hold_down_seconds: int\\n    - require_sustain_seconds: int (for non-reachability triggers)\\n  - safety:\\n    - require_approval: boolean (default true for prod initially)\\n    - max_flips_per_hour: int\\n    - max_traffic_shift_percent: int\\n    - rollback:\\n      - auto_rollback_enabled: boolean\\n      - rollback_after_seconds: int\\n      - rollback_require_healthy_primary_seconds: int\\n\\nE) Output schema\\nDecision output (single object, JSON):\\n- decision_id (stable hash of route_id + tenant_id + evaluation_time + policy_version)\\n- policy_version\\n- evaluation_time\\n- decision_type\\n- chosen_reason\\n- target_state (string encoding; owned by controller)\\n- requested_actions (string encoding; empty in recommend mode)\\n- evidence (string encoding; ordered)\\n- annotations (string encoding; includes thresholds, staleness, hold-down state)\\n\\nNote: In our implementation we\\u2019ll likely use structured objects, but for logging/audit we must generate a stable, versioned string representation.\\n\\nSafety constraints (ADR-043 alignment)\\n- Anti-flap:\\n  - Enforce hold-down between flips for non-reachability triggers.\\n  - Any rollback decision must respect a separate rollback hold-down (avoid ping-pong between primary and fallback).\\n- Rate limiting:\\n  - flip_budget_ok must be true, else HOLD.\\n- Approval hooks:\\n  - If require_approval is true, decision_type can still be FAILOVER but requested_actions must be empty and \\u201capproval_required=true\\u201d annotation set.\\n- Tenant/tier gates:\\n  - Enterprise/Dedicated can be configured with stricter \\u201cdo not cross data residency boundary\\u201d constraint (policy engine should surface \\u201cconstraint_violation:data_residency\\u201d rather than attempt partial shifts).\\n\\nEdge cases and expected behavior\\n1) Partial outage in primary region\\n- Reachability degraded (not down), 5xx burn elevated, capacity OK in fallback.\\n- Expected: PARTIAL_SHIFT (e.g., shift 25\\u201350% depending on max_traffic_shift_percent) if corroborated. If sustained and escalates to reachability down or error burn becomes severe => FAILOVER.\\n\\n2) Signal missing / ingestion delayed\\n- Any authoritative signal is stale beyond max_staleness_seconds.\\n- Expected: HOLD. Evidence must explicitly call out staleness and which signal blocked action.\\n\\n3) Fallback region constrained\\n- Primary is failing (5xx burn), fallback capacity_hard_gate true.\\n- Expected: HOLD + annotate \\u201cfallback_unhealthy_due_to_capacity\\u201d. Controller should invoke load shedding and retry-after rather than shifting load.\\n\\n4) Control plane degraded\\n- Control plane health degraded; data plane signals ambiguous.\\n- Expected: HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative. (Avoid flipping policies when control plane is suspect.)\\n\\n5) Multi-fallback selection\\n- If multiple eligible fallback regions are healthy, selection tie-breakers:\\n  1) policy-specified order\\n  2) lowest latency probe (if available in inputs)\\n  3) highest capacity headroom\\n  4) stable sort by region name\\n\\nTesting plan (draft)\\nUnit tests\\n- Determinism:\\n  - Same payload with randomized key order => same decision_id, decision_type, evidence ordering.\\n- Staleness gating:\\n  - Stale error burn + fresh reachability OK => HOLD.\\n- Priority:\\n  - Reachability DOWN overrides hold-down.\\n  - 5xx burn overrides latency burn when both exceed thresholds.\\n\\nIntegration tests\\n- Replay recorded signal snapshots from staging incidents + controlled game day traces.\\n- Validate output is compatible with controller dry-run UX (must contain reasons + evidence).\\n\\nPerformance considerations\\n- Evaluation must be cheap; do not add per-eval remote calls.\\n- Evidence strings must be bounded in size. Cap rejected_candidates and evidence list.\\n\\nOperational / observability hooks\\n- Emit a single log line per decision with:\\n  - decision_id, route_id, tenant_id (hashed in shared Hosted contexts), decision_type, chosen_reason\\n  - key thresholds and freshness\\n- Export metrics:\\n  - policy_engine_decisions_total{decision_type, chosen_reason, tier}\\n  - policy_engine_hold_reasons_total{reason}\\n  - policy_engine_eval_latency_ms\\n\\nOpen questions\\n- Exact shape of \\u201ctarget_state\\u201d string: should it be a controller-owned serialization of desired weights, or should the policy engine output high-level intent only?\\n- Do we want PARTIAL_SHIFT as a first-class decision type (recommended), or represent it as FAILOVER with weight < 100%?\\n- How strict should corroboration be for tail latency burn? (ADR-042 indicates corroboration required; we need the exact default set.)\\n- Where should data residency constraints live?\\n  - Option A: policy engine validates \\u201cregion set allowed\\u201d and blocks action.\\n  - Option B: upstream policy compilation prevents invalid eligible_regions.\\n\\nNear-term next steps\\n- Align with Miles/Ravi on canonical signal enum + reason enum.\\n- Draft schema PR for policy config additions (behind feature flag).\\n- Implement deterministic ordering + evidence output in policy engine.\\n- Wire to dry-run mode (ENG-2415) so the controller can display \\u201crecommended action + confidence + evidence\\u201d on game day.\\n\\nAppendix: candidate enums (WIP)\\nchosen_reason\\n- REACHABILITY_DOWN\\n- ERROR_BURN_FAST\\n- LATENCY_BURN_SUSTAINED\\n- CAPACITY_HARD_GATE\\n- SIGNALS_STALE\\n- HOLD_DOWN_ACTIVE\\n- FLIP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED\\n- CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION_DATA_RESIDENCY\\n- NO_HEALTHY_FALLBACK\\n\\nsignal_type\\n- REACHABILITY\\n- ERRORS_5XX_BURN\\n- TAIL_LATENCY_BURN\\n- CAPACITY_HEADROOM\\n- CONTROL_PLANE_HEALTH\\n\",\n  \"original_location\": \"google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_184be937d34a412ab5e61366d54d8ed6\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\nreachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity exhaustion).\n  - No first-class “hold-down” / dampening in evaluation; logic is split between policy rules and external controller.\n  - No consistent mechanism to enforce safety constraints per tenant/tier (max flips, blast radius caps, required approval).\n\nGoals\n- Add policy engine primitives so failover decisioning is:\n  - Deterministic and auditable (same inputs => same decision; explainability built-in).\n  - Compatible with ADR-042 (signal priority + corroboration) and ADR-043 (rollback + anti-flap).\n  - Safe by default (rate limits, required corroboration, blast radius constraints).\n- Support both:\n  - “Recommend” (dry-run) mode: compute candidate flips + evidence.\n  - “Enforce” mode: same evaluation but returns executable actions.\n\nNon-goals\n- Replace the automation controller. The controller still orchestrates execution, approvals, and cross-system workflow.\n- Re-architect signal ingestion. We consume normalized, time-bucketed signals from Region Health + SLO toolkit.\n- Build customer-facing UI here.\n\nTerminology\n- Policy: configuration describing routing behavior for a route/service/model/tier.\n- Region set: primary and fallback regions eligible for this route.\n- Trigger signal: normalized boolean or scalar indicating regional impairment or risk.\n- Decision: computed outcome (no-op, failover, partial shift, rollback, hold).\n- Action: executable change (policy flip, weight adjustment, circuit breaker mode) emitted by controller.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\nset: primary and fallback regions eligible for this route.\n- Trigger signal: normalized boolean or scalar indicating regional impairment or risk.\n- Decision: computed outcome (no-op, failover, partial shift, rollback, hold).\n- Action: executable change (policy flip, weight adjustment, circuit breaker mode) emitted by controller.\n\nInputs / data model assumptions\n- Policy engine receives inputs as a single evaluation payload, including:\n  - route_id (e.g., hosted.chat.completions, dedicated.pool.<pool_id>)\n  - tenant_id (optional for shared Hosted; required for Dedicated)\n  - tenant_tier (free/pro/enterprise/dedicated)\n  - current_routing_state (primary region, weights, last_flip_at)\n  - signals (per region, per signal type):\n    - reachability: ok|degraded|down + confidence + last_updated\n    - errors_5xx_burn: burn_rate + window + confidence\n    - tail_latency_burn: burn_rate + p95/p99 deltas + confidence\n    - capacity_headroom: percent + “hard gate” boolean\n    - control_plane_health (optional): ok|degraded|down\n  - evaluation_time (UTC epoch + monotonic sequence)\n  - constraints (policy-level + tenant-level): max_flips_per_hour, min_hold_down_seconds, require_approval, blast_radius_limit\n\nDeterminism requirements (core)\n1) Stable ordering\n- Evaluation must not depend on map iteration order.\n- Rule matching must define explicit ordering: by priority, then by tie-breakers.\n\n2) Stable time semantics\n- All windowed signals must be anchored to evaluation_time and include:\n  - effective_start, effective_end, and a “freshness” timestamp.\n- Engine must treat stale signals consistently:\n  - If authoritative signals are stale beyond threshold, decision = HOLD (do not fail over) unless reachability is explicitly DOWN with high confidence.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\ned signals must be anchored to evaluation_time and include:\n  - effective_start, effective_end, and a “freshness” timestamp.\n- Engine must treat stale signals consistently:\n  - If authoritative signals are stale beyond threshold, decision = HOLD (do not fail over) unless reachability is explicitly DOWN with high confidence.\n\n3) Single decision per evaluation\n- For a given (route_id, tenant_id, evaluation_time), engine emits exactly one decision object, even if multiple actions are possible.\n- Multi-step actions (e.g., drain -> shift weights -> finalize) must be represented as a sequence recommendation but still within a single decision record.\n\n4) Explainability\n- Decision must include:\n  - decision_type (NO_OP | FAILOVER | PARTIAL_SHIFT | ROLLBACK | HOLD)\n  - chosen_reason (canonical enum)\n  - evidence: ordered list of signals used, with values, freshness, and thresholds.\n  - rejected_candidates: (optional) top 1–3 alternatives and why they were not selected.\n\nProposed changes to policy engine\nA) New predicates / functions\n1) region_health(region, signal_type) -> {status, value, confidence, freshness_seconds}\n- Wrapper that pulls normalized data from payload and enforces freshness calculations.\n\n2) is_authoritative_reachability_down(region) -> bool\n- True only if:\n  - reachability.status == down\n  - confidence >= configured_min_confidence (default 0.9)\n  - freshness_seconds <= reachability_max_staleness (default 30s)\n\n3) burn_rate_exceeded(region, metric, window, threshold) -> bool\n- Works for errors_5xx_burn and tail_latency_burn.\n- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.\n\n4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool\n- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.\n- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\n- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.\n\n4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool\n- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.\n- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.\n\n5) corroborated(primary_signal, secondary_signal) -> bool\n- Enforces ADR-042 “required corroboration signals” when configured.\n- Example: if tail latency burn triggers, require either 5xx burn OR reachability degraded/down OR control plane degraded.\n\n6) hold_down_active(last_flip_at, min_hold_down_seconds) -> bool\n- If true, policy engine returns HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative.\n\n7) flip_budget_ok(tenant_id, route_id, max_flips_per_hour) -> bool\n- Input includes a precomputed counter from controller/state store (policy engine does not store state).\n\n8) blast_radius_ok(tenant_tier, requested_action) -> bool\n- Enforces “can’t shift more than X% traffic for tier Y without approval”.\n- For Hosted, blast radius is route-scoped; for Dedicated, pool-scoped.\n\nB) Deterministic evaluation mode (required)\n- Add an “evaluation_mode” field:\n  - recommend: compute decision + evidence; do not mark as executable\n  - enforce: compute decision; include explicit requested_action(s)\n- Engine must produce identical decision_type and evidence in both modes (action packaging differs).",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\nB) Deterministic evaluation mode (required)\n- Add an “evaluation_mode” field:\n  - recommend: compute decision + evidence; do not mark as executable\n  - enforce: compute decision; include explicit requested_action(s)\n- Engine must produce identical decision_type and evidence in both modes (action packaging differs).\n\nC) Signal hierarchy evaluation (ADR-042)\nPriority order (proposed canonical order for v1):\n1) Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback)\n2) Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity\n3) Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained\n4) Capacity exhaustion / hard gate => HOLD + load shed (controller action), avoid shifting into constrained region\n5) Control plane degradation => HOLD (do not flip rapidly; prevent oscillation)\n\nNotes:\n- “No healthy fallback” means every eligible fallback region fails capacity_hard_gate OR reachability is down OR stale beyond threshold.\n- If no healthy fallback, decision should be HOLD and include “degrade_allowed=true” hint (controller can activate load shedding / retry-after).\n\nD) Policy language / config schema additions\nAdd new fields (names tentative):\n- failover:\n  - enabled: boolean\n  - eligible_regions: [us-east, eu-west, ...]\n  - signal_requirements:\n    - primary_trigger: enum\n    - corroboration: [enum]\n    - min_confidence: float\n    - max_staleness_seconds: int\n  - dampening:\n    - min_hold_down_seconds: int\n    - require_sustain_seconds: int (for non-reachability triggers)\n  - safety:\n    - require_approval: boolean (default true for prod initially)\n    - max_flips_per_hour: int\n    - max_traffic_shift_percent: int\n    - rollback:\n      - auto_rollback_enabled: boolean\n      - rollback_after_seconds: int\n      - rollback_require_healthy_primary_seconds: int",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\n:\n    - require_approval: boolean (default true for prod initially)\n    - max_flips_per_hour: int\n    - max_traffic_shift_percent: int\n    - rollback:\n      - auto_rollback_enabled: boolean\n      - rollback_after_seconds: int\n      - rollback_require_healthy_primary_seconds: int\n\nE) Output schema\nDecision output (single object, JSON):\n- decision_id (stable hash of route_id + tenant_id + evaluation_time + policy_version)\n- policy_version\n- evaluation_time\n- decision_type\n- chosen_reason\n- target_state (string encoding; owned by controller)\n- requested_actions (string encoding; empty in recommend mode)\n- evidence (string encoding; ordered)\n- annotations (string encoding; includes thresholds, staleness, hold-down state)\n\nNote: In our implementation we’ll likely use structured objects, but for logging/audit we must generate a stable, versioned string representation.\n\nSafety constraints (ADR-043 alignment)\n- Anti-flap:\n  - Enforce hold-down between flips for non-reachability triggers.\n  - Any rollback decision must respect a separate rollback hold-down (avoid ping-pong between primary and fallback).\n- Rate limiting:\n  - flip_budget_ok must be true, else HOLD.\n- Approval hooks:\n  - If require_approval is true, decision_type can still be FAILOVER but requested_actions must be empty and “approval_required=true” annotation set.\n- Tenant/tier gates:\n  - Enterprise/Dedicated can be configured with stricter “do not cross data residency boundary” constraint (policy engine should surface “constraint_violation:data_residency” rather than attempt partial shifts).\n\nEdge cases and expected behavior\n1) Partial outage in primary region\n- Reachability degraded (not down), 5xx burn elevated, capacity OK in fallback.\n- Expected: PARTIAL_SHIFT (e.g., shift 25–50% depending on max_traffic_shift_percent) if corroborated. If sustained and escalates to reachability down or error burn becomes severe => FAILOVER.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\nability degraded (not down), 5xx burn elevated, capacity OK in fallback.\n- Expected: PARTIAL_SHIFT (e.g., shift 25–50% depending on max_traffic_shift_percent) if corroborated. If sustained and escalates to reachability down or error burn becomes severe => FAILOVER.\n\n2) Signal missing / ingestion delayed\n- Any authoritative signal is stale beyond max_staleness_seconds.\n- Expected: HOLD. Evidence must explicitly call out staleness and which signal blocked action.\n\n3) Fallback region constrained\n- Primary is failing (5xx burn), fallback capacity_hard_gate true.\n- Expected: HOLD + annotate “fallback_unhealthy_due_to_capacity”. Controller should invoke load shedding and retry-after rather than shifting load.\n\n4) Control plane degraded\n- Control plane health degraded; data plane signals ambiguous.\n- Expected: HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative. (Avoid flipping policies when control plane is suspect.)\n\n5) Multi-fallback selection\n- If multiple eligible fallback regions are healthy, selection tie-breakers:\n  1) policy-specified order\n  2) lowest latency probe (if available in inputs)\n  3) highest capacity headroom\n  4) stable sort by region name\n\nTesting plan (draft)\nUnit tests\n- Determinism:\n  - Same payload with randomized key order => same decision_id, decision_type, evidence ordering.\n- Staleness gating:\n  - Stale error burn + fresh reachability OK => HOLD.\n- Priority:\n  - Reachability DOWN overrides hold-down.\n  - 5xx burn overrides latency burn when both exceed thresholds.\n\nIntegration tests\n- Replay recorded signal snapshots from staging incidents + controlled game day traces.\n- Validate output is compatible with controller dry-run UX (must contain reasons + evidence).\n\nPerformance considerations\n- Evaluation must be cheap; do not add per-eval remote calls.\n- Evidence strings must be bounded in size.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/google_drive\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\nConnector: google_drive\nWorkspace: shared_drives\nTeam: eng-platform\n\nrecorded signal snapshots from staging incidents + controlled game day traces.\n- Validate output is compatible with controller dry-run UX (must contain reasons + evidence).\n\nPerformance considerations\n- Evaluation must be cheap; do not add per-eval remote calls.\n- Evidence strings must be bounded in size. Cap rejected_candidates and evidence list.\n\nOperational / observability hooks\n- Emit a single log line per decision with:\n  - decision_id, route_id, tenant_id (hashed in shared Hosted contexts), decision_type, chosen_reason\n  - key thresholds and freshness\n- Export metrics:\n  - policy_engine_decisions_total{decision_type, chosen_reason, tier}\n  - policy_engine_hold_reasons_total{reason}\n  - policy_engine_eval_latency_ms\n\nOpen questions\n- Exact shape of “target_state” string: should it be a controller-owned serialization of desired weights, or should the policy engine output high-level intent only?\n- Do we want PARTIAL_SHIFT as a first-class decision type (recommended), or represent it as FAILOVER with weight < 100%?\n- How strict should corroboration be for tail latency burn? (ADR-042 indicates corroboration required; we need the exact default set.)\n- Where should data residency constraints live?\n  - Option A: policy engine validates “region set allowed” and blocks action.\n  - Option B: upstream policy compilation prevents invalid eligible_regions.\n\nNear-term next steps\n- Align with Miles/Ravi on canonical signal enum + reason enum.\n- Draft schema PR for policy config additions (behind feature flag).\n- Implement deterministic ordering + evidence output in policy engine.\n- Wire to dry-run mode (ENG-2415) so the controller can display “recommended action + confidence + evidence” on game day.\n\nAppendix: candidate enums (WIP)\nchosen_reason\n- REACHABILITY_DOWN\n- ERROR_BURN_FAST\n- LATENCY_BURN_SUSTAINED\n- CAPACITY_HARD_GATE\n- SIGNALS_STALE\n- HOLD_DOWN_ACTIVE\n- FLIP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED\n- CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION_DATA_RESIDENCY\n- NO_HEALTHY_FALLBACK",

{
  "title": "Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation",
  "owner": "Jordan Lee",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json",
  "doc_type": "doc",
  "created_at": "2026-01-07",
  "last_modified": "2026-01-12",
  "collaborators": [
    "Ravi Menon",
    "Miles Thornton",
    "Benji Okafor",
    "Mina Haddad",
    "Ethan Park",
    "Allison Grant"
  ],
  "team": "eng-platform",
  "status": "draft",
  "tags": [
    "failover",
    "policy-engine",
    "determinism",
    "routing",
    "guardrails",
    "sre",
    "reliability-program"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "Linear: ENG-2411",
    "Linear: ENG-2412",
    "Linear: ENG-2415",
    "Linear: ENG-2416",
    "Confluence: adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy",
    "Confluence: adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback",
    "GitHub: redwood/pr-19812-policy-engine-signal-priority (planned)",
    "GitHub: redwood/pr-19815-routing-policy-rollback-safety (planned)"
  ],
  "content": "Context / why this exists
- We’re upgrading regional failover automation as part of Reliability Program (Q1–Q2 2026). Today, routing policy evaluation has a few gaps:
  - Non-deterministic behavior in edge cases (e.g., multiple signals firing, partial signal availability, time-window ambiguity).
  - Hard to reason about priority across trigger signals (reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity exhaustion).
  - No first-class “hold-down” / dampening in evaluation; logic is split between policy rules and external controller.
  - No consistent mechanism to enforce safety constraints per tenant/tier (max flips, blast radius caps, required approval).

Goals
- Add policy engine primitives so failover decisioning is:
  - Deterministic and auditable (same inputs => same decision; explainability built-in).
  - Compatible with ADR-042 (signal priority + corroboration) and ADR-043 (rollback + anti-flap).
  - Safe by default (rate limits, required corroboration, blast radius constraints).
- Support both:
  - “Recommend” (dry-run) mode: compute candidate flips + evidence.
  - “Enforce” mode: same evaluation but returns executable actions.

Non-goals
- Replace the automation controller. The controller still orchestrates execution, approvals, and cross-system workflow.
- Re-architect signal ingestion. We consume normalized, time-bucketed signals from Region Health + SLO toolkit.
- Build customer-facing UI here.

Terminology
- Policy: configuration describing routing behavior for a route/service/model/tier.
- Region set: primary and fallback regions eligible for this route.
- Trigger signal: normalized boolean or scalar indicating regional impairment or risk.
- Decision: computed outcome (no-op, failover, partial shift, rollback, hold).
- Action: executable change (policy flip, weight adjustment, circuit breaker mode) emitted by controller.

Inputs / data model assumptions
- Policy engine receives inputs as a single evaluation payload, including:
  - route_id (e.g., hosted.chat.completions, dedicated.pool.<pool_id>)
  - tenant_id (optional for shared Hosted; required for Dedicated)
  - tenant_tier (free/pro/enterprise/dedicated)
  - current_routing_state (primary region, weights, last_flip_at)
  - signals (per region, per signal type):
    - reachability: ok|degraded|down + confidence + last_updated
    - errors_5xx_burn: burn_rate + window + confidence
    - tail_latency_burn: burn_rate + p95/p99 deltas + confidence
    - capacity_headroom: percent + “hard gate” boolean
    - control_plane_health (optional): ok|degraded|down
  - evaluation_time (UTC epoch + monotonic sequence)
  - constraints (policy-level + tenant-level): max_flips_per_hour, min_hold_down_seconds, require_approval, blast_radius_limit

Determinism requirements (core)
1) Stable ordering
- Evaluation must not depend on map iteration order.
- Rule matching must define explicit ordering: by priority, then by tie-breakers.

2) Stable time semantics
- All windowed signals must be anchored to evaluation_time and include:
  - effective_start, effective_end, and a “freshness” timestamp.
- Engine must treat stale signals consistently:
  - If authoritative signals are stale beyond threshold, decision = HOLD (do not fail over) unless reachability is explicitly DOWN with high confidence.

3) Single decision per evaluation
- For a given (route_id, tenant_id, evaluation_time), engine emits exactly one decision object, even if multiple actions are possible.
- Multi-step actions (e.g., drain -> shift weights -> finalize) must be represented as a sequence recommendation but still within a single decision record.

4) Explainability
- Decision must include:
  - decision_type (NO_OP | FAILOVER | PARTIAL_SHIFT | ROLLBACK | HOLD)
  - chosen_reason (canonical enum)
  - evidence: ordered list of signals used, with values, freshness, and thresholds.
  - rejected_candidates: (optional) top 1–3 alternatives and why they were not selected.

Proposed changes to policy engine
A) New predicates / functions
1) region_health(region, signal_type) -> {status, value, confidence, freshness_seconds}
- Wrapper that pulls normalized data from payload and enforces freshness calculations.

2) is_authoritative_reachability_down(region) -> bool
- True only if:
  - reachability.status == down
  - confidence >= configured_min_confidence (default 0.9)
  - freshness_seconds <= reachability_max_staleness (default 30s)

3) burn_rate_exceeded(region, metric, window, threshold) -> bool
- Works for errors_5xx_burn and tail_latency_burn.
- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.

4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool
- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.
- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.

5) corroborated(primary_signal, secondary_signal) -> bool
- Enforces ADR-042 “required corroboration signals” when configured.
- Example: if tail latency burn triggers, require either 5xx burn OR reachability degraded/down OR control plane degraded.

6) hold_down_active(last_flip_at, min_hold_down_seconds) -> bool
- If true, policy engine returns HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative.

7) flip_budget_ok(tenant_id, route_id, max_flips_per_hour) -> bool
- Input includes a precomputed counter from controller/state store (policy engine does not store state).

8) blast_radius_ok(tenant_tier, requested_action) -> bool
- Enforces “can’t shift more than X% traffic for tier Y without approval”.
- For Hosted, blast radius is route-scoped; for Dedicated, pool-scoped.

B) Deterministic evaluation mode (required)
- Add an “evaluation_mode” field:
  - recommend: compute decision + evidence; do not mark as executable
  - enforce: compute decision; include explicit requested_action(s)
- Engine must produce identical decision_type and evidence in both modes (action packaging differs).

C) Signal hierarchy evaluation (ADR-042)
Priority order (proposed canonical order for v1):
1) Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback)
2) Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity
3) Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained
4) Capacity exhaustion / hard gate => HOLD + load shed (controller action), avoid shifting into constrained region
5) Control plane degradation => HOLD (do not flip rapidly; prevent oscillation)

Notes:
- “No healthy fallback” means every eligible fallback region fails capacity_hard_gate OR reachability is down OR stale beyond threshold.
- If no healthy fallback, decision should be HOLD and include “degrade_allowed=true” hint (controller can activate load shedding / retry-after).

D) Policy language / config schema additions
Add new fields (names tentative):
- failover:
  - enabled: boolean
  - eligible_regions: [us-east, eu-west, ...]
  - signal_requirements:
    - primary_trigger: enum
    - corroboration: [enum]
    - min_confidence: float
    - max_staleness_seconds: int
  - dampening:
    - min_hold_down_seconds: int
    - require_sustain_seconds: int (for non-reachability triggers)
  - safety:
    - require_approval: boolean (default true for prod initially)
    - max_flips_per_hour: int
    - max_traffic_shift_percent: int
    - rollback:
      - auto_rollback_enabled: boolean
      - rollback_after_seconds: int
      - rollback_require_healthy_primary_seconds: int

E) Output schema
Decision output (single object, JSON):
- decision_id (stable hash of route_id + tenant_id + evaluation_time + policy_version)
- policy_version
- evaluation_time
- decision_type
- chosen_reason
- target_state (string encoding; owned by controller)
- requested_actions (string encoding; empty in recommend mode)
- evidence (string encoding; ordered)
- annotations (string encoding; includes thresholds, staleness, hold-down state)

Note: In our implementation we’ll likely use structured objects, but for logging/audit we must generate a stable, versioned string representation.

Safety constraints (ADR-043 alignment)
- Anti-flap:
  - Enforce hold-down between flips for non-reachability triggers.
  - Any rollback decision must respect a separate rollback hold-down (avoid ping-pong between primary and fallback).
- Rate limiting:
  - flip_budget_ok must be true, else HOLD.
- Approval hooks:
  - If require_approval is true, decision_type can still be FAILOVER but requested_actions must be empty and “approval_required=true” annotation set.
- Tenant/tier gates:
  - Enterprise/Dedicated can be configured with stricter “do not cross data residency boundary” constraint (policy engine should surface “constraint_violation:data_residency” rather than attempt partial shifts).

Edge cases and expected behavior
1) Partial outage in primary region
- Reachability degraded (not down), 5xx burn elevated, capacity OK in fallback.
- Expected: PARTIAL_SHIFT (e.g., shift 25–50% depending on max_traffic_shift_percent) if corroborated. If sustained and escalates to reachability down or error burn becomes severe => FAILOVER.

2) Signal missing / ingestion delayed
- Any authoritative signal is stale beyond max_staleness_seconds.
- Expected: HOLD. Evidence must explicitly call out staleness and which signal blocked action.

3) Fallback region constrained
- Primary is failing (5xx burn), fallback capacity_hard_gate true.
- Expected: HOLD + annotate “fallback_unhealthy_due_to_capacity”. Controller should invoke load shedding and retry-after rather than shifting load.

4) Control plane degraded
- Control plane health degraded; data plane signals ambiguous.
- Expected: HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative. (Avoid flipping policies when control plane is suspect.)

5) Multi-fallback selection
- If multiple eligible fallback regions are healthy, selection tie-breakers:
  1) policy-specified order
  2) lowest latency probe (if available in inputs)
  3) highest capacity headroom
  4) stable sort by region name

Testing plan (draft)
Unit tests
- Determinism:
  - Same payload with randomized key order => same decision_id, decision_type, evidence ordering.
- Staleness gating:
  - Stale error burn + fresh reachability OK => HOLD.
- Priority:
  - Reachability DOWN overrides hold-down.
  - 5xx burn overrides latency burn when both exceed thresholds.

Integration tests
- Replay recorded signal snapshots from staging incidents + controlled game day traces.
- Validate output is compatible with controller dry-run UX (must contain reasons + evidence).

Performance considerations
- Evaluation must be cheap; do not add per-eval remote calls.
- Evidence strings must be bounded in size. Cap rejected_candidates and evidence list.

Operational / observability hooks
- Emit a single log line per decision with:
  - decision_id, route_id, tenant_id (hashed in shared Hosted contexts), decision_type, chosen_reason
  - key thresholds and freshness
- Export metrics:
  - policy_engine_decisions_total{decision_type, chosen_reason, tier}
  - policy_engine_hold_reasons_total{reason}
  - policy_engine_eval_latency_ms

Open questions
- Exact shape of “target_state” string: should it be a controller-owned serialization of desired weights, or should the policy engine output high-level intent only?
- Do we want PARTIAL_SHIFT as a first-class decision type (recommended), or represent it as FAILOVER with weight < 100%?
- How strict should corroboration be for tail latency burn? (ADR-042 indicates corroboration required; we need the exact default set.)
- Where should data residency constraints live?
  - Option A: policy engine validates “region set allowed” and blocks action.
  - Option B: upstream policy compilation prevents invalid eligible_regions.

Near-term next steps
- Align with Miles/Ravi on canonical signal enum + reason enum.
- Draft schema PR for policy config additions (behind feature flag).
- Implement deterministic ordering + evidence output in policy engine.
- Wire to dry-run mode (ENG-2415) so the controller can display “recommended action + confidence + evidence” on game day.

Appendix: candidate enums (WIP)
chosen_reason
- REACHABILITY_DOWN
- ERROR_BURN_FAST
- LATENCY_BURN_SUSTAINED
- CAPACITY_HARD_GATE
- SIGNALS_STALE
- HOLD_DOWN_ACTIVE
- FLIP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
- CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION_DATA_RESIDENCY
- NO_HEALTHY_FALLBACK

signal_type
- REACHABILITY
- ERRORS_5XX_BURN
- TAIL_LATENCY_BURN
- CAPACITY_HEADROOM
- CONTROL_PLANE_HEALTH

E) Output schema
Decision output (single object, JSON):
- decision_id (stable hash of route_id + tenant_id + evaluation_time + policy_version)
- policy_version
- evaluation_time
- decision_type
- chosen_reason
- target_state (string encoding; owned by controller)
- requested_actions (string encoding; empty in recommend mode)
- evidence (string encoding; ordered)
- annotations (string encoding; includes thresholds, staleness, hold-down state)

Note: In our implementation we’ll likely use structured objects, but for logging/audit we must generate a stable, versioned string representation.

Safety constraints (ADR-043 alignment)
- Anti-flap:
  - Enforce hold-down between flips for non-reachability triggers.
  - Any rollback decision must respect a separate rollback hold-down (avoid ping-pong between primary and fallback).
- Rate limiting:
  - flip_budget_ok must be true, else HOLD.
- Approval hooks:
  - If require_approval is true, decision_type can still be FAILOVER but requested_actions must be empty and “approval_required=true” annotation set.
- Tenant/tier gates:
  - Enterprise/Dedicated can be configured with stricter “do not cross data residency boundary” constraint (policy engine should surface “constraint_violation:data_residency” rather than attempt partial shifts).

Edge cases and expected behavior
1) Partial outage in primary region
- Reachability degraded (not down), 5xx burn elevated, capacity OK in fallback.
- Expected: PARTIAL_SHIFT (e.g., shift 25–50% depending on max_traffic_shift_percent) if corroborated. If sustained and escalates to reachability down or error burn becomes severe => FAILOVER.

Telemetry and logging guidance
- Emit these SDK-level metrics (tag by client_id and model):
  - stream_open_count (counter)
  - stream_close_count (counter)
  - stream_chunk_bytes (histogram)
  - stream_error_rate (counter + labels: error_type)
  - reconnect_attempts (counter)

- Log shape: JSON lines with these top-level fields: timestamp, client_id, model, request_id, event (open|chunk|error|close), chunk_index, chunk_size, latency_ms, netem_profile. Include sample log line in docs.

Common failure modes and canonical fixes
- Duplicate chunk ingestion:
  - Symptom: consumer observes identical text chunk twice after a reconnect.
  - Cause: server replay + client naive dedupe by content only.
  - Fix: SDK should attach and persist monotonic sequence tokens per stream (sequence_id + offset) and dedupe by (request_id, sequence_id, offset). If sequence metadata missing, fall back to content hashing with sliding window.

- Premature stream close on network blip:
  - Symptom: stream closes with HTTP 499 or socket reset during long generation.
  - Fix: implement soft-reconnect with resume token. Server supports resume token header X-Resume-Token. SDK steps:
    1) On transient network error, attempt_resume = true if resume token present.
    2) Reconnect with header X-Resume-Token: <token> and request resume range.

- Partial JSON messages (chunk boundary splits):
  - Symptom: JSON decoder failure in consumer when a JSON object is split across chunks.
  - Fix: SDK should buffer incomplete frames and only parse after assemble. Provide tolerant parser that recovers from trailing commas and whitespace.",

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- Reassembly and schema validation will run on the client side to avoid coupling streaming framing to a single server-side schema validator. We'll provide a lightweight incremental JSON accumulator that tolerates token boundaries (handles partial escape sequences and nested objects).
- For JS/TS we will leverage a small WASM-backed JSON streaming validator for common schemas to keep CPU down on large streams (optional, enabled by structured_schema).
- For Python and Go, the initial implementation will be pure-Python / pure-Go incremental parsers with targeted optimizations later.
- Security: tool invocation carry a request ID and signature; the shim will validate the tool_request envelope and ensure the client cannot spoof tool results.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests: >95% coverage in shim modules for each language.
- Integration tests: upstream runtime streaming harness exercising: tool_request lifecycle, partial structured-object reassembly, and sync-style iteration.
- Example apps: three minimal examples (TS, Py, Go) in the SDK repo under examples/incremental that compile and run in CI.
- Docs: canonical guide in docs/sdk/incremental.md with code snippets above and migration notes for existing customers.
- Backcompat safety: default behavior unchanged for existing clients unless they import the incremental module or set the opt-in flag.

Risks / Mitigations:
- Risk: partial-object parsing edge cases for deeply nested schemas -> Mitigation: add fuzz tests and a fallback reassembly mode that buffers until balanced braces appear for pathological cases.
- Risk: performance overhead on small messages -> Mitigation: add heuristics to bypass reassembly when structured_schema is absent.
- Risk: cross-language semantic drift -> Mitigation: cross-language conformance tests and example parity checks in CI.",

SDK can emit tool-call placeholders as 'delta' events (partial JSON). We recommend delimiting tool-call boundaries with a special token to avoid JSON streaming parse issues (e.g., '###TOOL-START' / '###TOOL-END'). Client libraries include a streaming JSON assembler to reconstruct tool payloads reliably.

Chat vs completions (tokenization & stop semantics):
- Chat (structured messages): token counting includes role tokens + separators. Stop sequences are applied to the final assembled assistant message. - Completions (single prompt): simpler token model; stop is applied server-side and attempts to end generation. Streaming sends token deltas identical to the final output tokens.

Billing notes: streaming is billed per emitted token; partial tokens and final tokens are deduplicated by token index for the same request.

Title: SDK Streaming and Network Simulator Playbook
Source: EnterpriseRAG/confluence

Connector: confluence

bash
  docker compose -f docker-compose.ci.yml up -d netem-proxy redwood-mock-api
  export REDWOOD_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8080
  pytest tests/integration/test_streaming.py::test_stream_resilience --maxfail=1 -q

Telemetry and logging guidance
- Emit these SDK-level metrics (tag by client_id and model):
  - stream_open_count (counter)
  - stream_close_count (counter)
  - stream_chunk_bytes (histogram)
  - stream_error_rate (counter + labels: error_type)
  - reconnect_attempts (counter)

- Log shape: JSON lines with these top-level fields: timestamp, client_id, model, request_id, event (open|chunk|error|close), chunk_index, chunk_size, latency_ms, netem_profile. Include sample log line in docs.

Common failure modes and canonical fixes
- Duplicate chunk ingestion:
  - Symptom: consumer observes identical text chunk twice after a reconnect.
  - Cause: server replay + client naive dedupe by content only.
  - Fix: SDK should attach and persist monotonic sequence tokens per stream (sequence_id + offset) and dedupe by (request_id, sequence_id, offset). If sequence metadata missing, fall back to content hashing with sliding window.

- Premature stream close on network blip:
  - Symptom: stream closes with HTTP 499 or socket reset during long generation.
  - Fix: implement soft-reconnect with resume token. Server supports resume token header X-Resume-Token. SDK steps:
    1) On transient network error, attempt_resume = true if resume token present.
    2) Reconnect with header X-Resume-Token: <token> and request resume range.

- Partial JSON messages (chunk boundary splits):
  - Symptom: JSON decoder failure in consumer when a JSON object is split across chunks.
  - Fix: SDK should buffer incomplete frames and only parse after assemble. Provide tolerant parser that recovers from trailing commas and whitespace.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- Reassembly and schema validation will run on the client side to avoid coupling streaming framing to a single server-side schema validator. We'll provide a lightweight incremental JSON accumulator that tolerates token boundaries (handles partial escape sequences and nested objects).
- For JS/TS we will leverage a small WASM-backed JSON streaming validator for common schemas to keep CPU down on large streams (optional, enabled by structured_schema).
- For Python and Go, the initial implementation will be pure-Python / pure-Go incremental parsers with targeted optimizations later.
- Security: tool invocation carry a request ID and signature; the shim will validate the tool_request envelope and ensure the client cannot spoof tool results.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests: >95% coverage in shim modules for each language.
- Integration tests: upstream runtime streaming harness exercising: tool_request lifecycle, partial structured-object reassembly, and sync-style iteration.
- Example apps: three minimal examples (TS, Py, Go) in the SDK repo under examples/incremental that compile and run in CI.
- Docs: canonical guide in docs/sdk/incremental.md with code snippets above and migration notes for existing customers.
- Backcompat safety: default behavior unchanged for existing clients unless they import the incremental module or set the opt-in flag.

Risks / Mitigations:
- Risk: partial-object parsing edge cases for deeply nested schemas -> Mitigation: add fuzz tests and a fallback reassembly mode that buffers until balanced braces appear for pathological cases.
- Risk: performance overhead on small messages -> Mitigation: add heuristics to bypass reassembly when structured_schema is absent.
- Risk: cross-language semantic drift -> Mitigation: cross-language conformance tests and example parity checks in CI.

Messages: Sanjay: Quick question — iterator resume semantics when a streaming transport degrades to polling. Do we require an opaque resumable token from the service, or should the SDK try to reconstruct progress locally? Thinking about Python/TS/Go ergonomics and cross-language parity.
Olga: Clarify the failure mode: connection drop during an open stream vs server explicitly telling us to switch to poll? Those feel different for retries/resume policies.
Sanjay: Mostly connection drop / transient network + occasional model fallback (stream unsupported -> switch to poll). Both matter. We want minimal client code changes for app authors.
Mike: Option A: server issues an opaque resume_token that SDK passes back to restart; simple for SDKs but ties us to server token format and lifecycle. Option B: server exposes stable per-item cursor (e.g. monotonic index) so SDK can resume from index. Option C: full idempotent item IDs + dedupe on client.
Olga: Token size/durability concerns: opaque token can embed KV cache pointers (fast) but might leak internal identifiers. Also tokens can grow large if they include chunked state.
Elaine: From retries perspective: if we expose internal automatic retries + resume, SDKs will hide complexity, but we must be explicit about backoff and max-resume attempts. If SDK retries forever apps will be surprised.
Sanjay: For language ergonomics: Python iterator API should be minimal: `for item in client.stream(...):` — adding a mandatory resume param feels awkward. For TS/Go we can expose the same opt-in field but keep default autop-retry.
Sanjay: small sketch (Python):
```py
it = client.stream("/chat", prompt)
# after a disconnect
new_it = client.stream("/chat", prompt, resume_token=it.resume_token)
```
TS sketch:
```ts
const it = client.stream(...);
// it.resumeToken() ?
await client.stream(..., { resumeToken: it.resumeToken() })
```
Mike: If we use `it.resume_token` accessor, languages differ on async-safety: TS may need a promise, Python attribute ok. Go

Source: EnterpriseRAG/slack

Connector: slack

/health
# -> 200 {"ok":true,"model_status":"ready"}
```
SDK (404):
```
await client.embeddings.health()
# -> throws 404 Not Found
```
The sampleapp calls embeddings.health during startup and falls back to a heavy probe loop when the SDK 404s.

igor: ugh. For A we should treat numeric-like strings as numbers for those specific params. But we also don't want to silently accept totally invalid strings. Suggestion: heuristic coercion only for fields listed in a small whitelist (max_tokens, timeout_ms, top_k). Log a warning when coercion happens.

maya: +1. Add a lightweight coercion layer before validation: if param expects integer and value is a string of digits, coerce. Also update quickstart docs to show preferred input types.

igor: for B we likely shipped the embeddings.health route after the last SDK release. Two fixes: (1) add embeddings.health to SDK surface in the next patch, (2) make the SDK return a clearer error when endpoint missing (hint: "endpoint may not be available in this SDK version; check server API or upgrade SDK").

noah: another subtle streaming mismatch: REST streams a chunk that begins with a newline when the model emits formatted markdown, but the Node SDK trims leading newlines from the first chunk before delivering to the app — so users see delayed newline. First-time devs think streaming is dropping characters.

maya: that's nasty. We should preserve chunk boundaries exactly for the first N bytes and avoid trimming. Add an e2e streaming test that asserts first chunk integrity.

igor: also spotted a race with auth refresh: SDK background refresh swaps tokens mid-stream causing a 401 on the next chunk; our retry logic then resends the entire request which results in duplicate side-effects for non-idempotent endpoints. Recommendation: don't retry streaming/mutating requests automatically after mid-stream 401. Instead surface a clear error and expose an option to use idempotency-key or resume tokens for safe retries.

SDK ergonomics (JS/TS first-pass):
- Low-level: createStream(opts) returns AsyncIterable<Frame> and a controller with methods: send() (for client frames), requestResume(token), setWindow(bytes). This is for advanced use.
- High-level: StreamClient.open({schema, onText, onStruct, onTool, onCheckpoint, onError}) where handlers are simple sync/async functions. The SDK will manage checksums, resume attempts, and flow-control automatically.
- Tool registration: client.registerTool({id, handler: (params) => Promise<Result>, timeout}) - SDK routes TOOL_CALL frames to handlers. If no handler, SDK buffers until app decides.
- Validation mode: open|partial|strict. In partial mode, SDK emits onStruct events when enough path fragments arrive. In strict mode, SDK will attempt to reconstruct and run schema validation and emit error frames if mismatch.

Backpressure and latency tradeoffs: 
- Default client window 64KB. If app needs lower latency, pass max_window_bytes=8KB.
- SDK will apply jittered retries on resume to avoid thundering herd.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Checkpoints should not include PII. If model output contains sensitive info, servers should redact before embedding into resume checksums.
- Tool-calls may include secrets in params; SDK must mark them ephemeral and not persist them in local storage unless explicitly requested by the app.
- Resume tokens must be signed and short-lived; no server-side sticky state required.

Telemetry and observability (minimal):
- Events: stream.open, stream.resume_attempt, stream.resume_success, stream.resume_fail, tool.call, validation.failure, flow_control_change, stream.close.
- Recommended sample rates: resume events 100%, validation failures 100%, text_chunk histograms 1% by default.

SDK can emit tool-call placeholders as 'delta' events (partial JSON). We recommend delimiting tool-call boundaries with a special token to avoid JSON streaming parse issues (e.g., '###TOOL-START' / '###TOOL-END'). Client libraries include a streaming JSON assembler to reconstruct tool payloads reliably.

Chat vs completions (tokenization & stop semantics):
- Chat (structured messages): token counting includes role tokens + separators. Stop sequences are applied to the final assembled assistant message. For streaming, partial deltas may not respect stop sequences until the 'done' event; clients should implement local heuristics for early truncation when stop tokens are emitted in deltas.
- Completions (single prompt): simpler token model; stop is applied server-side and attempts to end generation. Streaming sends token deltas identical to the final output tokens.

Billing notes: streaming is billed per emitted token; partial tokens and final tokens are deduplicated by token index for the same request.
--- excerpt end ---

I can convert the excerpt into a short 'streaming contract' JSON schema if we want to push it to them tomorrow.

reordered reconnections, and concurrent reconnections from multiple client IPs.

## Design Links

- https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SeqAnchor+SSE+design+doc
  - https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1s3SeqAnchor/proto-dumps

## Implementation Notes

- Protocol: add header X-Seq-Token on initial handshake; server will include 'anchor' SSE events with type=anchor and payload: {seq, boundary_type, boundary_id, checksum}.
  - Chunk envelope: each data chunk will be JSONL with fields: seq, offset, payload, checksum; payload may include function_call frames encoded separately and tagged with boundary_id.
  - Retention: keep last N anchors and associated chunks per stream; default retention window is 30s or 1MB. Configurable per-customer on Dedicated plans.
  - Resume logic: on reconnect with X-Seq-Resume, server validates seq and serves minimal replay window; if seq expired, fallback to full stream restart and emit 'resume_lost' event.
  - Idempotency for tool-calls: server assigns call-dedup-id for each function invocation; replays will not re-execute calls if dedup-id already seen—call status persisted to short-lived call cache with TTL aligned to retention window.
  - Compatibility shim: if client lacks resume headers, server emits a 'compat-v1' framing header and anchors will be no-op markers so older clients can ignore but preserve stream integrity.
  - Observability: emit telemetry events for resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_expired, anchor_emitted with stream_id and token; add dashboard panel in Console runtime-1.24.
  - API changes: SDKs (JS/Python/Go) will get helper util to persist resume token and transparently attempt resume; default enabled for hosted API, opt-out via client config.

(surface)
- Minimal calls: PrefetchManifest.upload(manifest), Handshake.status(session_token) and Cancel(prefetch_id). Rationale: small surface to maintain language SDK simplicity and reduce integration cost.
- SDKs expose local cache hooks: onManifestAccepted(metadata), onPrefetchProgress(percent), onFallback(reason).

Streaming interplay and structured output
- Manifest-driven prefetch allows server to start incremental partial outputs earlier (e.g., emit an initial structured header saying which tools are ready and which are degraded).
- Structured tool-calling frames include an optional prefetch.confirmation block that client SDK can use to render optimistic UI.

Telemetry and signals
- New metrics: prefetch.accept_rate, prefetch_hit_rate (per manifest entry), prefetch_latency_ms, prefetch_waste_tokens.
- Instrumentation: add prefetch.* tags to tracing spans and integrate with Console dashboards and Optimize recommendations.

Security and privacy
- Manifests may include private resource hints. Treat manifests as user data subject to retention/policy. Provide per-manifest privacy_tier: public|sensitive|restricted. Use KMS tagging for restricted prefetch jobs.

SDK ergonomics notes
- Lightweight: keep binary size small for mobile by providing manifest helpers as optional module.
- Backward compatible: manifest calls are optional; server falls back to default routing when absent.
- Offline-first: SDK should cache last manifest and attempt opportunistic prefetch when device is charging/wi-fi. Provide TTLs to prevent stale prefetches.

Operational concerns and rollout
- Canary feature flags per-customer to gate prefetch routing and billing. Initial limited rollout to 5 pilot customers.
- Billing: optional discounted prefetch token bucket (customer-paid) vs on-demand prefetch paid from normal usage. Need billing experiment.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How to best express unknown/conditional flows (e.g., tool called only if search yield > 0)? Consider boolean predicates vs lightweight branching hints.
- Should prefetch be charged immediately or only when consumed? Need finance input (JIRA:PRIC-432).

The server tracks speculative lifecycles and exposes a cancel token when the definitive execution path is ready. 2) Latency-empathy frames: Streaming protocol augmented with optional meta-frames that carry estimated time-to-completion (ETC), partial confidence scores, and minimal structured placeholders. Clients can use these frames to show progressive UI: skeleton text, provisional action buttons, or a disabled tool preview. 3) Tool-call split execution: Separate "prepare" and "execute" phases for tool calls. 'prepare' runs a light-weight validation and stub response (schema + sample output) to return within low-latency window. 'execute' runs the full tool and returns definitive result. SDK surface exposes both phases with clear idempotency and reconciliation helpers. 4) Structured streaming + schema patches: Instead of a single JSON blob at the end, the model emits typed patch frames (op-add, op-replace) which the SDK assembles and validates incrementally. Patch frames contain a short validation hint; server runs background strict validation and emits a final 'seal' frame. SDKs should surface both the assembled object and the stream of ops for apps that want optimistic UI. API/Protocol Sketch: - HTTP/WS streaming envelopes: { frame_type, payload_type, payload, meta } where frame_type in [text_delta, schema_op, tool_stub, tool_result, meta_eta]. (Note: this doc intentionally uses prose; final spec will be precise.) - Prefetch mode flag on request: prefetch_mode: none | conservative | speculative. Conservative: only try cached prefixes and small continuation windows (<=64 tokens). Speculative: may spawn a lightweight continuation model. - Tool handshake: client request can include tool_lifecycle=prepare|execute and correlation_id. Server returns a tool_stub frame with {schema, sample, stub_id} then later a tool_result frame with {stub_id, result, provenance}. Of Scope

- Runtime implementation details (ENG tickets will own kernel/runtime changes).
  - Telemetry schema overhaul — only minimal telemetry for compatibility decisions will be added.
  - Language-specific ergonomic reworks beyond the handshake surface (e.g., async API refactors) unless required for the contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1) Handshake: All three SDKs implement an HTTP/2 header-based handshake and WS fallback that includes: sdk-version, requested-features, preferred-stream-mode, and idempotency-capability. Test vectors exist in sdk-compat-suite.
  - 2) Graceful downgrade: When server replies with a reduced feature set, SDKs must: emit a single telemetry event, translate streaming to polling/paginated fallback without data loss (when possible), and surface a single typed warning to application developers within one second of connection establishment.
  - 3) Streaming resume: For long-lived streams, the handshake must negotiate a resume-token format. SDKs must be able to persist a resume token (opaque string) and resume within 30s of disconnection with at-most-once semantics for already-delivered units, documented per-language.
  - 4) Pagination & cursors: Cursor format changes must be supported via versioned cursor namespaces. SDKs must detect unknown cursor namespaces and either attempt a server-side translation endpoint (if advertised) or fail with a deterministic error code and recovery steps.
  - 5) Retry/backoff contract: SDKs implement a standard retry window algorithm: honor Retry-After and Retry-Quota headers, default to exponential backoff with jitter, and expose a hook for apps to override. End-to-end tests must validate behavior under 429/503 and partial stream failures.
  - 6) Compatibility matrix: sdk-compat-suite must cover all permutations of (SDK version ±2, runtime version ±1) across streaming/pagination/retry features with pass/fail indicators. Tests run in CI against canary and stable runtime images.
  - 7) Docs & migration: Publish PRD + short migration guide in Confluence and code snippets for each SDK. Docs
