- Use bootstrapped CIs for delta_quality_vs_baseline; require 95% CI lower bound > -0.03 for quick gate (i.e., we need to be 95% confident candidate is not worse than -3%).

This PR introduces a probabilistic cohort prober and a resilience scheduler that jointly allocate probe budget across cohort slices and adapt probe intensity based on short-term stability signals.\n\nWhat this changes: Implements a cohort-aware prober that: 1) partitions traffic into probabilistic cohorts by request fingerprint and configurable slicing rules, 2) samples per-cohort probes with adjustable risk scores, and 3) emits structured probe telemetry for downstream canary evaluators. Adds a resilience scheduler that: 1) maintains a rolling budget ledger per-cohort, 2) uses an annealing-based throttle to reduce probe rate when regressions are suspected, and 3) exposes safety gates (latency delta and error ratio thresholds) to automatically pause probes or trigger reroute.\n\nDesign notes: The prober uses a configurable \"seeded\" RNG so runs can be reproduced in replay mode. Cohort scoring combines recent latency variance, request weight, and rollout stage to compute a probe utility. The scheduler applies an exponential backoff with decay and a small probabilistic allowance so that probes still sample the cohort at reduced rate (avoids blind spots). The ledger tracks both tokens (probe budget) and a cooldown credit to support bursty but limited probing.\n\nTesting and CI: Added unit tests for cohort selection, deterministic seeding, scheduler budget arithmetic, and a short integration test that runs a synthetic mixed workload (two cohorts with different qps and p95). Telemetry schema updated with probe events and shed reasons. CI workflow updated to include a lightweight perf-canary job that runs the integration test in the matrix. approach is sampled probes with cached probe state per-tenant to limit cost.
  - We will prioritize 'low-volume, high-sensitivity' tenants for initial gates (legal/compliance customers).
  - Backwards compatibility: default safety-lane is empty so existing rollouts remain unchanged until configured.

## Rollout Plan

- Phase 0: feature flag behind runtime + controller flags, internal test tenants only
  - Phase 1: enable safety-lane for 10 internal tenants and run synthetic probes for 48h
  - Phase 2: extend to 50 customers + enable automatic rollback at score < 0.6 for 5m window
  - Phase 3: public release with templates for common tenant cohorts and Console integrations

## Test Plan

- Unit: probe scoring library + routing matcher
  - Integration: end-to-end simulation (simulated tenants, spike failure scenarios, region outage): assert correct spillback and no cross-tenant contamination
  - Performance: measure added 95th tail latency for safety-lane checks under 5% baseline
  - Chaos: memory pressure + kernel slowdowns to validate degraded fallback behaviour

## Metrics

- per-tenant canary pass-rate
  - compatibility-score distribution (p10/p50/p90)
  - rollbacks triggered by probe-score vs by capacity loss
  - cross-tenant contamination incidents (should be 0)

## Risk Mitigation

- Sampling probes rather than probing every request to bound cost and latency impact
  - Grace period in rollout controller: require sustained failure for 5m before auto-rollback
  - Circuit-breaker: if tier capacity falls below 30% use conservative spillback policy
  - Manual override: ops can force traffic fencing toggle per-tenant via control-plane API

emits structured audit events for console and runbooks.
- Add shadowing toggles for parallel probing of candidate variants without impacting live split.
- Provide an auto-rollback policy with hysteresis and graduated backoff to avoid flapping.
- Expose diagnostic endpoints and Grafana panels for per-step metrics and rationale.

Design highlights and novel ideas:
- "Safepoints": explicit named checkpoints in a rollout where non-reversible expansion requires additional approval or stronger signals. Safepoints can be configured as time-based or metric-based.
- "Horizon decay": a configurable attenuation function that slows traffic growth if variance in key metrics increases; helps prevent step overshoot for bursty workloads.
- Quality-aware splits: traffic weights can be dynamically rebalanced by integrating a lightweight quality signal (e.g., rerank drift or semantic similarity) for A/B tests.
- Shadow probes: sampled requests are mirrored to candidate variants with separate budget accounting; failures in the shadow path do not affect the live split but surface in the supervisor's risk score.

Acceptance criteria:
1) POST /rollouts accepts new spec and validates schema, including safepoints and attenuation curve.
2) Supervisor advances steps automatically when configured SLOs are met for a configurable consecutive window, and pauses when the guardrail is violated.
3) Automatic rollback triggers when sustained regression (configurable window) exceeds threshold; rollback includes a cooldown to prevent immediate reattempt.
4) Shadowing mode can be enabled per-route and produced mirrored telemetry tracked independently.
5) E2E integration tests added that simulate latency spikes, error bursts, and quality regressions and assert supervisor behavior.
6) Grafana dashboard with per-step metrics and an "explain" view (why step advanced/paused/rolled back).

result.text:
[Document context]
Title: Probabilistic cohort prober and resilience scheduler for gradual-rollout guards
Source: EnterpriseRAG/github

Connector: github

shapes. Current canary probes use uniform sampling and a single probe budget which results in either missed regressions on small cohorts or too aggressive probes that increase noise. This PR introduces a probabilistic cohort prober and a resilience scheduler that jointly allocate probe budget across cohort slices and adapt probe intensity based on short-term stability signals.

What this changes: Implements a cohort-aware prober that: 1) partitions traffic into probabilistic cohorts by request fingerprint and configurable slicing rules, 2) samples per-cohort probes with adjustable risk scores, and 3) emits structured probe telemetry for downstream canary evaluators. Adds a resilience scheduler that: 1) maintains a rolling budget ledger per-cohort, 2) uses an annealing-based throttle to reduce probe rate when regressions are suspected, and 3) exposes safety gates (latency delta and error ratio thresholds) to automatically pause probes or trigger reroute.

Design notes: The prober uses a configurable "seeded" RNG so runs can be reproduced in replay mode. Cohort scoring combines recent latency variance, request weight, and rollout stage to compute a probe utility. The scheduler applies an exponential backoff with decay and a small probabilistic allowance so that probes still sample the cohort at reduced rate (avoids blind spots). The ledger tracks both tokens (probe budget) and a cooldown credit to support bursty but limited probing.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for cohort selection, deterministic seeding, scheduler budget arithmetic, and a short integration test that runs a synthetic mixed workload (two cohorts with different qps and p95). Telemetry schema updated with probe events and shed reasons. CI workflow updated to include a lightweight perf-canary job that runs the integration test in the matrix. The branch initially had a flaky test (timing-sensitive) which was hardened by switching to time-mock injections; subsequent CI runs passed.

Simulation / sanity checks before running live evals:
- Run bootstrap resampling on the sampled set to estimate CI for delta_quality. If CI crosses hard_threshold frequently, mark as unstable and increase sample allocation.
- Monte Carlo simulate expected production impact by re-weighting weighted_delta_quality by production_pct_est to produce an expected user impact score in expected users/day lost-equivalent. Convert to $ impact using revenue/retention heuristics (Sheet: CostModel).

Quality metric guidance (slice-specific):
- Not every slice uses the same automated metric. Map slice->metric in Slices Registry.
- For generative tasks prefer embedding-based similarity + human spot-check. For classification use precision/recall and per-class breakdown. For retrieval or reranking use NDCG/Recall@k.

Practical heuristics & shortcuts (we use these day-to-day):
- "Alpha gating": For early experiments with small budgets use stricter MQPD thresholds to avoid false positives (more conservative).
- "Delta-sign filter": if delta_cost is tiny (<1% savings) require stronger quality evidence before recommending.
- "Escalation path": any regression where the example contains PII or legal text auto-triggers security review.

Experiment tracking columns (for the minimal ticket):
- experiment_id (string), config_id, run_id, started_at, finished_at, engineer, baseline_hash, variant_hash, total_tokens, total_cost_est, pass_rate, top_failed_examples (comma-separated prompt_ids), link_to_raw_results

Rollout playbook (after PASS):
- Stage 0: Canary at 1% traffic for 24 hours with slice-level alarms.
- Stage 1: Canary 10% for 48 hours, run full slice checks again via lightweight streaming evaluation.
- Stage 2: 50% with rollback window and automatic fallback to baseline on error rate bump.",

score.
- Decision score (DS): a normalized scalar computed from heatmap aggregates that maps to GO / CAUTION / HOLD / ROLLBACK actions.
- Tiered slice: pre-defined group of probes that share an SLO (e.g., CriticalTenantFlows, BillingIntents, LowRiskExplorations).

Inputs required
---------------
1) Heatmap snapshot covering the last N hours (default N=24) with per-probe metrics: total_calls, failure_count, avg_severity, median_latency_ms, embedding_drift_score.
2) Active rollout plan metadata: target model id, variant (quantized/float16), percent_traffic, scheduled_start.
3) Baseline reference heatmap from the control population (previous model or canary).
4) SLO manifest for target slices (SLO window, allowed error budget, latency SLO).
5) Operational constraints: maintenance windows, capacity headroom, and dependency map.

Decision scoring algorithm (summary)
----------------------------------
We compute three sub-scores and aggregate them into DS (range 0..100):

- StabilityScore (SS): weighted failure density normalized by probe priority. Formula: SS = 100 * sum_p (w_p * (failure_count_p / max(1,total_calls_p))) / sum_p(w_p)
- LatencyPenalty (LP): 10 * max(0, (median_latency_ms - latency_slo_ms) / latency_slo_ms) clipped at 30
- DriftFactor (DF): 50 * embedding_drift_score_95pct_quantile normalized against baseline drift

Final Decision Score: DS = clamp(SS + LP + DF, 0, 100)

Action mapping (recommended)
---------------------------
- DS <= 15: GO (promote / continue rollout)
- 15 < DS <= 35: CAUTION (slow rollout to 10% and schedule targeted human review within 4 hours)
- 35 < DS <= 60: HOLD (pause rollout; trigger automated bisect & focused probes)
- DS > 60: ROLLBACK (automatically revert to baseline variant and open incident ticket)",

Description: Create an automated, auditable workflow to safely decommission old model variants while minimizing customer disruption. This yields interpretable slices like: "short-answer-hallucination-sensitive", "long-form-low-risk", "multi-turn-chat-mid-length".

Metrics (definitions used here):
- Semantic Perturbation Score (SPS): 0–100 scale derived from entailment + embedding similarity + normalized token overlap; lower is worse. We report delta = quantized minus fp16.
- Prompt Robustness Index (PRI): percentage of runs where the top-3 completions overlap by >=0.7 cosine and operator acceptability; captures stability to sampling and numeric instability.
- Hallucination Drift Rate (HDR): fraction of responses with unsupported factual claims relative to a small knowledge oracle (wiki-snapshot) — flagged by our internal hallucination detector.
- Latency and token-cost deltas included but considered secondary for this doc.

Methodology (concise):
- Prompt set: 1,200 prompts selected from onboarding pool (balanced by product route and historical failure log).
- Runs: 5 seeds per prompt with sampling settings matching production (temperature 0.2–0.7 depending on route), deterministic evaluation for QA slices where applicable.
- Post-process: automatic metrics + 300 human spot checks (stratified across slices).
- Hardware: A100 fp16 baseline; quantized models executed on testbench nodes with kernels closest to production environment.

Detailed per-slice notes (selected slices with notable deltas):
1) short-answer-hallucination-sensitive
   - SPS delta: AWQ-8 -2.1, GPTQ-8 -3.0, int8 -4.5, int4 -12.8
   - PRI delta: AWQ -3%, GPTQ -6%, int8 -8%, int4 -28%
   - HDR: AWQ +1.8ppt, GPTQ +3

Content: Purpose and intent:
This is an operational notebook for running short-lived, high-signal experiments we call "epochs". An epoch is a timeboxed cross-functional rollout designed to test a single mounted change (model variant, routing policy, quantization profile, caching tweak). The goal here is to capture play-by-play decisions, risk assessment, and a reproducible rollback template for fast reversion if observed risk exceeds thresholds.

High-level principles (working):
- Keep cohort sizes intentionally small for first epoch; prefer multiple staggered micro-epochs over one sweeping exposure.
- Attach a numeric risk score to each epoch before activation and re-evaluate live.
- Make a rollback decision language explicit and automated where possible (API flags + alert hooks).
- Prioritize user-visible quality metrics first, then infra signals.

Definitions (terms we use in this doc):
- Epoch: short experiment window (1–48 hours) with fixed cohort slices.
- Micro-cohort: 0.1%–2% of traffic from a targeted routing slice (region, account tier).
- Risk score: 0–100 composite calculated from quality, latency, error, and business signal deltas.
- Cumulative regret budget: allocated tolerance for negative delta before hard rollback.

Pre-activation checklist (must pass all soft gates):
- Ownership: Eng lead and Product owner confirmed in PR and rollout form.
- Tickets & artifacts: PR linked, smoke tests green (link), canary infra configured (flag + experiment id).
- Reference eval: static prompt set and automated oracle scoring for output quality (baseline stored).
- Monitoring hooks: dashboards created (P50/P95 latency, 5xx rate, cost-per-token, eval drift), alert thresholds wired.
- Communication: announcement posted to #rollouts-ops with experiment id, slices, and rollback window.

.
- Should require explicit acknowledgment in UI (“Apply anyway” with staged rollout suggested).

We should also have a “Not rated” state
- For cases with insufficient telemetry, misconfigured metrics, or suggestion type requiring missing prerequisites.
- UI should not show a risk badge; show “Insufficient data” instead.

How risk gets computed (high level; intended for internal alignment)
We’re deciding between two things:
A) A simple rules-based mapping (fast to ship, explainable)
B) A numeric score 0–100 mapped to bands (more flexible, risk of opacity)

Current preference for beta: rules-based mapping, with an internal numeric score retained for diagnostics.

Candidate inputs
Latency:
- Baseline p50/p95/p99 over last 7d (or 14d if 7d is sparse)
- Predicted deltas for p50/p95 and “tail multiplier” (p95 delta vs p50 delta)
- Share of requests already near SLA threshold (if customer defines SLO; otherwise use Redwood route defaults)

Reliability / queueing:
- Peak concurrency estimate and burstiness (p95 QPS / median QPS)
- Current queue time contribution (if available) / saturation signals
- Recent timeout rate (baseline) and any correlated spikes

Confidence:
- Telemetry coverage: fraction of traffic instrumented + retention window
- Stability: how much workload changed week-over-week (e.g., seq length distribution drift)
- Model/route eligibility: whether the model/runtime supports the recommended technique equivalently

Guardrail flags (hard overrides)

2) Severity dimensions and scoring inputs

Severity is derived from three orthogonal dimensions: impact, incidence, and reproducibility. Each dimension is scored 0–4 and then converted to a combined severity band (S1 - S5). The dimensions are defined as: 

- Impact (0–4): how customer-visible and harmful the failure is. 0 = negligible UI noise; 4 = data loss, privacy breach, or dangerous advice.
- Incidence (0–4): fraction of requests/samples that exhibit the failure in the measured slice. 0 = rare (<=0.01%); 4 = pervasive (>20%).
- Reproducibility (0–4): how reliably a human/automated replay can reproduce the failure. 0 = non-deterministic single-flaky outputs; 4 = deterministic on replayed inputs or deterministic in production telemetry.

- Reproducibility: 4 = 100% deterministic upon replay with same seeds/temperature; 3 = reproducible majority of replays; 2 = reproducible only with specific contexts/priming; 1 = flaky across runs; 0 = appears once in noisy long-tail.

Source: EnterpriseRAG/github

ac_drift (default off) - [x] migration to create audit_fingerprint_shards table (backfill limited to 7 days) - [x] staged rollout to internal infra then canary tenants then wide release - [x] notify SOC and SRE channels and add alert templates for high-confidence drifts

Operational notes: The detector computes an evidence_score (0-100) using weighted signals: unexpected-allow-events, failed-authentication-probes, KMS-region-mismatch, rate-of-change in bindings. The KMS explainer outputs a short human-friendly justification per anomalous key event (example: "CMK arn:... used by service-account:svc-ingest in region eu-west-1, tenant claim shows region=us-east-1 => possible cross-region routing via proxy-operator"). The fingerprint indexer normalizes audit payloads (removes ephemeral request IDs, normalizes caller ids, canonicalizes resource ARNs) and stores a 64-bit fingerprint which is used to group events quickly in the web UI and in the alert payloads.

Migration and data retention: The migration creates a rolling 7-day backfill by default to limit storage and risk; teams can request longer retention via support. The migration is reversible (drops index shards) if rollback triggered. Backfill runs are rate-limited and instrumented to avoid load spikes on the audit store.

Security considerations: The new services run in a restricted operator role with read-only audit-store permissions and explicit deny for key-decrypt operations. We added an operator-bound KMS wrapper to ensure the analyzer never exports raw key material; only metadata (key id, region, usage counters) are stored. All artifacts are covered by existing audit pipelines and the new audit_fingerprint_shards table is encrypted-at-rest and access-controlled via RBAC v2 templates.

ellen (Analytics): We'll need a quality gate: A/B on top-100 customer prompts, quality delta v baseline <= 8%. I can run synthetic evals during canary.
drew (Eng): Timeline impact: shim + flag + basic telemetry = 2 sprints if we parallelize. Full reranker = sprint+2. Risk: corner cases in ordering under high prefix overlap.
alex (Eng-Platform): Canary config (we can automate):

result.text:
[Document context]
Title: Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol
Source: EnterpriseRAG/confluence
Path: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/probe-heatmap-rollout-decision-protocol-2024.json
Connector: confluence
Workspace: applied-ml-and-evals

score.
- Decision score (DS): a normalized scalar computed from heatmap aggregates that maps to GO / CAUTION / HOLD / ROLLBACK actions.
- Tiered slice: pre-defined group of probes that share an SLO (e.g., CriticalTenantFlows, BillingIntents, LowRiskExplorations).

Inputs required
---------------
1) Heatmap snapshot covering the last N hours (default N=24) with per-probe metrics: total_calls, failure_count, avg_severity, median_latency_ms, embedding_drift_score.
2) Active rollout plan metadata: target model id, variant (quantized/float16), percent_traffic, scheduled_start.
3) Baseline reference heatmap from the control population (previous model or canary).
4) SLO manifest for target slices (SLO window, allowed error budget, latency SLO).
5) Operational constraints: maintenance windows, capacity headroom, and dependency map.

Decision scoring algorithm (summary)
----------------------------------
We compute three sub-scores and aggregate them into DS (range 0..100):

- StabilityScore (SS): weighted failure density normalized by probe priority. Formula: SS = 100 * sum_p (w_p * (failure_count_p / max(1,total_calls_p))) / sum_p(w_p)
- LatencyPenalty (LP): 10 * max(0, (median_latency_ms - latency_slo_ms) / latency_slo_ms) clipped at 30
- DriftFactor (DF): 50 * embedding_drift_score_95pct_quantile normalized against baseline drift

Final Decision Score: DS = clamp(SS + LP + DF, 0, 100)

Action mapping (recommended)
---------------------------
- DS <= 15: GO (promote / continue rollout)
- 15 < DS <= 35: CAUTION (slow rollout to 10% and schedule targeted human review within 4 hours)
- 35 < DS <= 60: HOLD (pause rollout; trigger automated bisect & focused probes)
- DS > 60: ROLLBACK (automatically revert to baseline variant and open incident ticket)

.
- SIA: aligned=100, neutral=60, mismatch=20.

Composite score computation: 
- For each signal S_i produce normalized value v_i in 0..100.
- Composite = sum_i (w_i * v_i) / sum(w_i)  -> normalized 0..100

Risk buckets (thresholds):
- Green: Composite >= 65 -> low immediate risk. Playbook: light-touch cadences, automated renewal nudges 90/45/14 days.
- Amber: Composite 40-64 -> medium risk. Playbook: schedule review with CSM, run focused adoption campaign, check billing/contract notes, escalate to solutions if KFA low.
- Red: Composite < 40 -> high risk. Playbook: immediate senior review, Executive sponsor outreach, on-site or technical health check, seat audit.

Top-3 driver extraction:
- Compute per-signal contribution = w_i * (100 - v_i) for negatively oriented signals (where lower is worse), or w_i * (v_i if higher is worse for some signals). Sort descending to show the top contributors to risk. Include a short natural-language reason for each driver.

Status: In Progress

Assignee: Liam Novak

Project: Model Onboarding & Lifecycle

Cycle: 2025-W05

Estimate: 5

## Labels

- deprecation
  - model-onboarding
  - pinning
  - migration-assistant
  - observability

## Dependencies

- ENG-21456
  - PM-20456

Release: runtime-1.20

Security Review Required: false

Description: Create an automated, auditable workflow to safely decommission old model variants while minimizing customer disruption. Deliverables: a compatibility validator service that scores customer workloads against candidate replacement models; an in-console staged migration assistant that suggests pins, SDK compatibility shims, and rollout windows; standardized customer notices and automated signal-driven scheduling for phased retirements.

## Background

- We frequently onboard new model variants and need a reproducible, low-touch way to retire older weights without breaking customers who relied on subtle behavior differences.
  - Existing playbooks are fragmented across PM guides and engineering runbooks; customers occasionally hit silent regressions after model swaps or get surprised by sudden EoL notices.
  - Goal: reduce manual ops required from Solutions/Success teams and provide data-driven migration recommendations tied to published performance profiles.

## Goals

- Provide a compatibility score (0-100) per customer workload comparing retiring variant -> candidate replacement using eval prompt suites and embedding drift metrics.
  - Expose an in-console migration assistant that surfaces low-risk & high-risk customers and generates migration suggestions (pin, gradual rollout, compatibility shim).
  - Automate customer-facing notices with templated content and link directly to migration guides and SDK warnings.
  - Publish performance profile diffs prominently in model catalog to make trade-offs explicit.

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Cross-SDK: unify streaming handshake, consumer ergonomics, and auth/retry semantics (Python/TS/Go)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/github\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/github/pr-95312-unify-handshake-consumer-ux-and-retry-bump.json\nConnector: github\nWorkspace: pr-95312-unify-handshake-consumer-ux-and-retry-bump.json\n\n: 1) a minimal, consistent 3-way auth handshake for stream starts and reconnects; 2) a small, opinionated consumer surface that makes backpressure and heartbeats explicit but ergonomic; 3) a single, test-backed retry policy and token-refresh hook that avoids duplicate requests during auth rotation.\n\nSummary of changes (high level):\n- Introduce a lightweight stream handshake: CLIENT_HELLO -> AUTH_OK -> SERVER_READY. Implemented in each SDK with shared semantics and compatibility fallbacks for older servers.\n- Consumer ergonomics: new thin abstraction that replaces ad-hoc iterators/callbacks. Python exposes StreamConsumer (AsyncIterator + context manager) with buffer_size and heartbeat_ack semantics; TS exposes createStreamConsumer({onMessage, onComplete, bufferSize}) and an async iterable wrapper; Go exposes StreamReader(ctx) that implements io.Reader-like semantics for single-message reads and a Cancel() helper.\n- Auth/retries: unified RetryWithAuthRefresh policy across SDKs. Retries are jittered exponential with token refresh hook invoked once per logical request; transparent idempotency guard added for non-idempotent unary calls.\n- Backwards compatibility: consumers detect old handshake flows and fall back to legacy behavior for servers that do not return AUTH_OK. Migration warnings are surfaced at runtime (single warn log per process).\n- Tests: added unit tests for handshake transitions and integration e2e stream tests in a local harness that simulates mid-stream token expiration.\n- Version bumps: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 0.8.3.\n\nWhy this shape: the platform-level serving runtime already relies on explicit stream lifecycle events; exposing a small, consistent surface across SDKs reduces footguns (double-sends during reauth, leaked goroutines or pending async generators) and improves observability for consumers.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Cross-SDK: unify streaming handshake, consumer ergonomics, and auth/retry semantics (Python/TS/Go)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/github\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/github/pr-95312-unify-handshake-consumer-ux-and-retry-bump.json\nConnector: github\nWorkspace: pr-95312-unify-handshake-consumer-ux-and-retry-bump.json\n\n.0, go 0.8.3.\n\nWhy this shape: the platform-level serving runtime already relies on explicit stream lifecycle events; exposing a small, consistent surface across SDKs reduces footguns (double-sends during reauth, leaked goroutines or pending async generators) and improves observability for consumers.\n\nMigration notes:\n- Python: replace raw async for msg in client.stream() with: async with client.stream_consumer() as c: async for msg in c: ...; short-lived code paths still supported but deprecated.\n- TS: prefer createStreamConsumer over stream().iterator() when you need backpressure controls.\n- Go: use NewStreamReader(ctx) to ensure reads cancel cleanly on token refresh.\n\nChecklist: \n- [x] Cross-SDK API proposals agreed with SDK leads (Raj/Elena)\n- [x] Unit + integration tests added\n- [x] CI flake triaged and rerun (see CI summary)\n- [x] Changelog & migration guide updated\n\nNotes: this PR intentionally keeps signal surface minimal (3 flags + 2 callbacks) to avoid burdening consumers. See linked Linear ENG-2142 for design doc.\n\n## Commits\n\n- a1f3b9d: sdk: add handshake primitives and shared test harness\n  - b4e2c10: python: StreamConsumer implementation, tests and deprecation warnings\n  - c7d9f21: typescript: createStreamConsumer, iterable adapter and examples\n  - d2a7eba: go: NewStreamReader + cancel semantics and integration test\n  - f1b5c30: common: retry-with-auth-refresh policy and idempotency guard\n  - e3c8f5a: docs: migration guide and changelogs for python/ts/go\n\n## Files Changed",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Cross-SDK: unify streaming handshake, consumer ergonomics, and auth/retry semantics (Python/TS/Go)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/github\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/github/pr-95312-unify-handshake-consumer-ux-and-retry-bump.json\nConnector: github\nWorkspace: pr-95312-unify-handshake-consumer-ux-and-retry-bump.json\n\na7eba: go: NewStreamReader + cancel semantics and integration test\n  - f1b5c30: common: retry-with-auth-refresh policy and idempotency guard\n  - e3c8f5a: docs: migration guide and changelogs for python/ts/go\n\n## Files Changed\n\n- redwood-sdk-python/redwood/streaming/consumer.py\n  - redwood-sdk-python/tests/test_stream_handshake.py\n  - redwood-sdk-typescript/src/stream/consumer.ts\n  - redwood-sdk-typescript/examples/streaming-backpressure.md\n  - redwood-sdk-go/stream/reader.go\n  - redwood-sdk-go/stream/read_test.go\n  - shared/sdk/auth/retry_policy.go\n  - shared/sdk/auth/retry_policy_test.go\n  - docs/migration/streaming-migration.md\n  - CHANGELOGs/SDKs.md\n  - tools/test-harness/stream-proxy-sim.js\n\n## Review Comments\n\n- Raj: Can we avoid a second token refresh race if two concurrent streams call the hook? Suggest ensuring the hook is single-flight per token_id. Response: implemented singleflight guard in shared retry_policy with metrics (auth_refresh_locks).\n  - Elena: TS consumer ergonomics look good but question on buffer default. Response: default buffer_size changed to 16 and documented rationale (latency vs memory).\n  - Samir: Go Cancel() semantics — will it leak goroutines when Cancel is called mid-read? Response: added explicit test and closed goroutine via consistent context cancellation path; verified in go race run.\n  - CI-bot: e2e streaming failed when simulating token expiry. {
  "repo": "redwood",
  "pr_number": "95312",
  "title": "Cross-SDK: unify streaming handshake, consumer ergonomics, and auth/retry semantics (Python/TS/Go)",
  "author": "Maya Chen",
  "created_at": "2026-02-18",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-24",
  "merged_at": "2026-02-24",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "feature/sdk-cross-handshake-consumer-ergonomics",
  "reviewers": [
    "Raj Patel",
    "Elena Kuznetsova",
    "Samir Nair"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "sdk",
    "streaming",
    "auth",

  "linked_linear": [
    "ENG-2142",
    "ENG-2178"
  ],
  "linked_jira": [
    "SUP-312"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "11",
  "additions": "642",
  "deletions": "211",
  "description": "Motivation: We have diverging streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go SDKs and subtle auth-retry edge cases that manifest as half-open streams or token race conditions during refresh. This PR unifies three areas: 1) a minimal, consistent 3-way auth handshake for stream starts and reconnects; 2) a small, opinionated consumer surface that makes backpressure and heartbeats explicit but ergonomic; 3) a single, test-backed retry policy and token-refresh hook that avoids duplicate requests during auth rotation.\n\nSummary of changes (high level):\n- Introduce a lightweight stream handshake: CLIENT_HELLO -> AUTH_OK -> SERVER_READY. Implemented in each SDK with shared semantics and compatibility fallbacks for older servers.\n- Consumer ergonomics: new thin abstraction that replaces ad-hoc iterators/callbacks. Python exposes StreamConsumer (AsyncIterator + context manager) with buffer_size and heartbeat_ack semantics; TS exposes createStreamConsumer({onMessage, onComplete, bufferSize}) and an async iterable wrapper; Go exposes StreamReader(ctx) that implements io.Reader-like semantics for single-message reads and a Cancel() helper.\n- Auth/retries: unified RetryWithAuthRefresh policy across SDKs. Retries are jittered exponential with token refresh hook invoked once per logical request; transparent idempotency guard added for non-idempotent unary calls.\n- Backwards compatibility: consumers detect old handshake flows and fall back to legacy behavior for servers that do not return AUTH_OK. Migration warnings are surfaced at runtime (single warn log per process).\n- Tests: added unit tests for handshake transitions and integration e2e stream tests in a local harness that simulates mid-stream token expiration.\n- Version bumps: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 0.8.3.\n\nWhy this shape: the platform-level serving runtime already relies on explicit stream lifecycle events; exposing a small, consistent surface across SDKs reduces footguns (double-sends during reauth, leaked goroutines or pending async generators) and improves observability for consumers.\n\nMigration notes:\n- Python: replace raw async for msg in client.stream() with: async with client.stream_consumer() as c: async for msg in c: ...; short-lived code paths still supported but deprecated.\n- TS: prefer createStreamConsumer over stream().iterator() when you need backpressure controls.\n- Go: use NewStreamReader(ctx) to ensure reads cancel cleanly on token refresh.\n\nChecklist: \n- [x] Cross-SDK API proposals agreed with SDK leads (Raj/Elena)\n- [x] Unit + integration tests added\n- [x] CI flake triaged and rerun (see CI summary)\n- [x] Changelog & migration guide updated\n\nNotes: this PR intentionally keeps signal surface minimal (3 flags + 2 callbacks) to avoid burdening consumers. See linked Linear ENG-2142 for design doc.",
  "commits": [
    "a1f3b9d: sdk: add handshake primitives and shared test harness",
    "b4e2c10: python: StreamConsumer implementation, tests and deprecation warnings",
    "c7d9f21: typescript: createStreamConsumer, iterable adapter and examples",
    "d2a7eba: go: NewStreamReader + cancel semantics and integration test",
    "f1b5c30: common: retry-with-auth-refresh policy and idempotency guard",
    "e3c8f5a: docs: migration guide and changelogs for python/ts/go"
  ],
  "files_changed": [
    "redwood-sdk-python/redwood/streaming/consumer.py",
    "redwood-sdk-python/tests/test_stream_handshake.py",
    "redwood-sdk-typescript/src/stream/consumer.ts",
    "redwood-sdk-typescript/examples/streaming-backpressure.md",
    "redwood-sdk-go/stream/reader.go",
    "redwood-sdk-go/stream/read_test.go",
    "shared/sdk/auth/retry_policy.go",
    "shared/sdk/auth/retry_policy_test.go",
    "docs/migration/streaming-migration.md",
    "CHANGELOGs/SDKs.md",
    "tools/test-harness/stream-proxy-sim.js"
  ],
  "review_comments": [
    "Raj: Can we avoid a second token refresh race if two concurrent streams call the hook? Suggest ensuring the hook is single-flight per token_id. Response: implemented singleflight guard in shared retry_policy with metrics (auth_refresh_locks).",
    "Elena: TS consumer ergonomics look good but question on buffer default. Response: default buffer_size changed to 16 and documented rationale (latency vs memory).",
    "Samir: Go Cancel() semantics \u2014 will it leak goroutines when Cancel is called mid-read? Response: added explicit test and closed goroutine via consistent context cancellation path; verified in go race run.",
    "CI-bot: e2e streaming failed when simulating token expiry. Author: added extra wait/retry in harness and hardened backoff; reran and passed."
  ],
  "ci_checks": [
    "unit (python/ts/go): pass",
    "lint (python/ts/go): pass",
    "integration (stream e2e harness): initial fail (token race) -> fix -> pass",
    "e2e (smoke): pass",
    "security-scan: pass"
  ],
  "merge_method": "squash",
  "merge_outcome": "merged",
  "release_notes": "- SDKs: unify streaming handshake semantics across Python/TS/Go; introduce ergonomic StreamConsumer/StreamReader abstractions.\n- Auth: single-flight token refresh hook and unified RetryWithAuthRefresh policy to avoid duplicate in-flight retries.\n- Backwards compatibility: servers without AUTH_OK are supported with harmless warnings.\n- Version bumps: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 0.8.3.\n- Migration guidance added to docs/migration/streaming-migration.md",
  "breaking_change": "false",
  "notes_for_release_manager": "This is a cross-SDK change: coordinate SDK package publishes in the same release window to avoid mixed-version consumer code paths. Defer rollout of deprecation warnings for 2 weeks after release.",

Title: Cross-SDK: unify streaming handshake, consumer ergonomics, and auth/retry semantics (Python/TS/Go)
Source: EnterpriseRAG/github

: 1) a minimal, consistent 3-way auth handshake for stream starts and reconnects; 2) a small, opinionated consumer surface that makes backpressure and heartbeats explicit but ergonomic; 3) a single, test-backed retry policy and token-refresh hook that avoids duplicate requests during auth rotation.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Introduce a lightweight stream handshake: CLIENT_HELLO -> AUTH_OK -> SERVER_READY. Implemented in each SDK with shared semantics and compatibility fallbacks for older servers.
- Consumer ergonomics: new thin abstraction that replaces ad-hoc iterators/callbacks. Python exposes StreamConsumer (AsyncIterator + context manager) with buffer_size and heartbeat_ack semantics; TS exposes createStreamConsumer({onMessage, onComplete, bufferSize}) and an async iterable wrapper; Go exposes StreamReader(ctx) that implements io.Reader-like semantics for single-message reads and a Cancel() helper.
- Auth/retries: unified RetryWithAuthRefresh policy across SDKs. Retries are jittered exponential with token refresh hook invoked once per logical request; transparent idempotency guard added for non-idempotent unary calls.
- Backwards compatibility: consumers detect old handshake flows and fall back to legacy behavior for servers that do not return AUTH_OK. Migration warnings are surfaced at runtime (single warn log per process).
- Tests: added unit tests for handshake transitions and integration e2e stream tests in a local harness that simulates mid-stream token expiration.
- Version bumps: python 0.12.0, typescript 1.9.0, go 0.8.3.

Why this shape: the platform-level serving runtime already relies on explicit stream lifecycle events; exposing a small, consistent surface across SDKs reduces footguns (double-sends during reauth, leaked goroutines or pending async generators) and improves observability for consumers.

AE/Ethan running evaluation; SE Priya leading POC. CSM Liam looped for contract terms if we convert.\n\nKey quote from CTO on 2026-01-12 demo call: \"We need guaranteed isolation + audit trail before legal will sign — SOC2 plus SAML is non-negotiable.\"\n\nPOC summary: 2-week hosted POC validated KB embeddings and reranking quality (recall + precision acceptable).   "notes": "Account: mid-market analytics SaaS. Product: customer-facing search + support assistant. Started with hosted API trial (Jan) to validate embeddings quality and cost profile, now moving to Dedicated/VPC for predictable latency and data isolation. AE/Ethan running evaluation; SE Priya leading POC. CSM Liam looped for contract terms if we convert.\n\nKey quote from CTO on 2026-01-12 demo call: \"We need guaranteed isolation + audit trail before legal will sign \u2014 SOC2 plus SAML is non-negotiable.\"\n\nPOC summary: 2-week hosted POC validated KB embeddings and reranking quality (recall + precision acceptable). Next stage: 4-week Dedicated POC in customer VPC (Redwood Dedicated) to test autoscale, KV cache warm-start, and p95 latency under 50 concurrent chat sessions.\n\nSecurity ask list (provided to Redwood 2026-01-20): SOC2 Type II report, SSO/SAML metadata exchange, audit log retention policy, KMS integration pattern, data residency confirmation for US-EAST and EU regions, deletion+retention controls for user data. Legal expects redlined contract with standard security addenda.\n\nProcurement note: Budgeting ~ $120k-$180k ARR depending on committed capacity. CPO indicated willingness to sign annual commit if SLA meets p95 < 800ms for chat at target concurrency. Cost sensitivity: moderate; willing to trade slight cost for determinism (dedicated pools).\n\nInternal flags: SE asked for quantized model guidance \u2014 which model/quantization profile hits p95 targets vs token cost. Priya requested a recommended config by 2026-02-11.\n\nStubs: Drive deck (pricing + POC runbook), Fireflies for demo + security walkthrough, Jira tickets for infra questions.\n",
  "recent_activities": [
    "2026-01-08: Intro discovery call (AE Ethan) \u2014 identified primary use-cases and data sensitivity",
    "2026-01-12: Hosted API demo + Fireflies transcript \u2014 validated generation quality for support flows",
    "2026-01-20: Security questionnaire submitted (customer) \u2014 SOC2 + SSO emphasized",
    "2026-01-28: Tech deep-dive w/SE (Priya) on Dedicated architecture \u2014 discussed KV cache and autoscale",
    "2026-02-02: Pricing refresh email from AE with committed capacity tiers \u2014 customer asked for example SLOs",
    "2026-02-05: SAML test scheduling call; Priya to provide ADFS metadata"
  ],
  "use_case_summary": "Primary: support virtual agent that answers product docs and tickets using embeddings + reranking. Secondary: internal doc search for product teams. Must support multi-tenant routing, region residency for EU customers, and maintain audit trail of inference requests. Latency SLOs target p95 < 800ms for chat, embeddings throughput ~200 req/s for nightly batch indexing. Will start on hosted API for quick validation then move to Dedicated/VPC for stability and compliance.",
  "poc_details": "Planned Dedicated POC: 4 weeks. Goals: validate p95 latency under concurrency (50 users), verify KV cache warm-up, test model fallback behavior, run penetration test on VPC endpoints, validate audit log fidelity and retention policy (1 year). Deliverables: perf report, security evidence pack (SOC2 excerpt, SAML logs), cost projection for 12-month commit.",
  "security_review_notes": "Legal/security requires: SOC2 Type II report (latest), SAML/SSO integration guide, audit log schema and retention controls, KMS integration approach (customer-managed keys preferred), data residency statement for EU region, and proof of physical access controls for Dedicated hardware. Customer requested an attested runbook for incident response and access revocation timeline.",
  "next_steps_details": "1) Redwood to supply SOC2 evidence bundle + SAML metadata by 2026-02-11. 2) SE to deliver model/quantization recommendation and target config (Priya) by 2026-02-11. 3) Schedule Dedicated POC kickoff (tentative 2026-02-15) pending security sign-off. 4) Procurement to confirm budget and commit band by 2026-05.",
  "additional_context": "Customer has enterprise customers in EU \u2014 data residency and auditability are driving the Dedicated requirement. They prefer minimal vendor lock-in; asked about exportable model snapshots and KV cache persistence. They are evaluating pricing against Anthropic/Vertex for committed capacity. Redwood's differentiation: clearer observability (token-level cost breakdown) and routing/fallback options were called out positively in demo.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Executive OKRs: headcount allocation checklist & freeze exceptions\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/gmail\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/gmail/michael_grant/20270530-executive-okrs-headcount-allocation-checklist.json\nConnector: gmail\nWorkspace: michael_grant\n\n- From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>\\nTo: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com\\nDate: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700\\nSubject: Executive OKRs: headcount allocation checklist & freeze exceptions\\n\\nTeam —\\n\\nQBR prep note: the execs want a clean headcount allocation table tied to our OKRs by the end of next week. I've attached QBR_headcount_model_v2.xlsx (baseline + two scenarios). Please do the following and reply in-thread by EOD Friday (06/04):\\n\\n1) For your org, list up to three hires you consider top-priority for hitting current OKRs (name the role, justification tied to specific OKR, expected start quarter).\\n2) Flag any backfills that are must-fill vs can-wait. Include cost delta (annual fully-loaded) if possible.\\n3) If you need an exception to the hiring freeze, complete the attached freeze-exception-form.pdf and include a 2–3 line business impact statement.\\n4) Note any dependencies (tools, infra, vendor spend) that materially change the hire economics.\\n\\nI'm particularly focused on: Serving/runtime (latency OKR), Platform (reliability SLO), and Sales (net-new ARR). We have a constrained budget scenario (see tab: Scenario B) — if you can provide prioritized trade-offs (e.g., freeze swap a junior SWE for a senior infra engineer), include them.\\n\\nI'll consolidate and bring a single slide for execs on Monday's leadership sync.\\n\\nThanks —\\nMichael Grant\\nHead of Strategy & Ops\\nRedwood Inference\\n[Attachment: QBR_headcount_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]\\n\n  - From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>\\nTo: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>\\",

  "thread_id": "mg-20270530-exec-okrs-headcount-001",

  "subject": "Executive OKRs: headcount allocation checklist & freeze exceptions",
  "participants_internal": [
    "michael_grant",
    "laura_bennett",
    "marissa_cole",
    "markus_klein",
    "vanessa_ortiz",
    "vivek_kulkarni"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "Karen Li <karen.li@acmecorp.com>",
    "Pegasus Talent <talent@pegasushr.com>"
  ],
  "message_count": "6",
  "first_email_at": "2027-05-30T08:12:00-07:00",
  "last_email_at": "2027-05-31T11:02:00-07:00",

  "related_account": "AcmeCorp",
  "region": "us",
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "QBR_headcount_model_v2.xlsx",
    "freeze-exception-form.pdf",
    "cap_impact_summary.pdf"
  ],
  "related_links": [
    "https://hubspot.redwood/deal/ACME-4582",
    "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2BqQ-HeadcountModels"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>\\nTo: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com\\nDate: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700\\nSubject: Executive OKRs: headcount allocation checklist & freeze exceptions\\n\\nTeam \u2014\\n\\nQBR prep note: the execs want a clean headcount allocation table tied to our OKRs by the end of next week. I've attached QBR_headcount_model_v2.xlsx (baseline + two scenarios). Please do the following and reply in-thread by EOD Friday (06/04):\\n\\n1) For your org, list up to three hires you consider top-priority for hitting current OKRs (name the role, justification tied to specific OKR, expected start quarter).\\n2) Flag any backfills that are must-fill vs can-wait. Include cost delta (annual fully-loaded) if possible.\\n3) If you need an exception to the hiring freeze, complete the attached freeze-exception-form.pdf and include a 2\u20133 line business impact statement.\\n4) Note any dependencies (tools, infra, vendor spend) that materially change the hire economics.\\n\\nI'm particularly focused on: Serving/runtime (latency OKR), Platform (reliability SLO), and Sales (net-new ARR). We have a constrained budget scenario (see tab: Scenario B) \u2014 if you can provide prioritized trade-offs (e.g., freeze swap a junior SWE for a senior infra engineer), include them.\\n\\nI'll consolidate and bring a single slide for execs on Monday's leadership sync.\\n\\nThanks \u2014\\nMichael Grant\\nHead of Strategy & Ops\\nRedwood Inference\\n[Attachment: QBR_headcount_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]\\n",
    "From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>\\nTo: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>\\nCc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com\\nDate: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Executive OKRs: headcount allocation checklist & freeze exceptions\\n\\nThanks Michael \u2014\\n\\nQuick intake from Talent (high level):\\n- Current pipeline: 9 active offers across Eng/PS/Sales, 4 expected acceptances in June.\\n- Time-to-fill median: 42 days for IC engineering roles; senior infra roles trending to 70 days.\\n- Immediate backfills: 3 (one in PS, one in Platform infra, one IC in Serving) \u2014 recommending \\\"must-fill\\\" for Platform infra backfill (critical SLO owner).\\n- Freeze exceptions: prepping 2 forms now (one for Platform infra, one for AE quota-carrying role) \u2014 will attach completed freeze-exception-form.pdf in follow-up.\\n\\nAttached are comments on the model (QBR tab annotations). For cost deltas I used midpoint comp assumptions; if finance has updated burdens, please call them out.\\n\\nLaura Bennett\\nDirector, Talent Operations\\nRedwood Inference\\n[Attachment: freeze-exception-form.pdf (pdf)]\\n\\nOn Sun, 30 May 2027 at 08:12, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> Team \u2014\\n> ...\\n",
    "From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>\\nTo: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com\\nCc: Karen Li <karen.li@acmecorp.com>\\nDate: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Executive OKRs: headcount allocation checklist & freeze exceptions\\n\\nAdding Sales perspective \u2014\\n\\nTop-priority hires for H2 (Sales):\\n- Senior AE (quota-carrying) \u2014 tied to OKR: +$5M expansion by EOY; near-term pipeline includes ACME renewal which needs renewed exec engagement (Karen Li looped). Expected Q3 start.\\n- Sales Engineer (pre-sales) \u2014 supports Platform and Serving pitch; high leverage for net-new.\\n\\nBackfills: AE backfill for a departing rep is high-priority (lose seat = measurable ARR risk). We are willing to accept a 6-week lag but prefer immediate hire. Freeze exception form attached (Laura has it).\\n\\nKaren \u2014 thanks for sharing the renewal timeline earlier; we're baking that into our ask.\\n\\nMarissa Cole\\nVP, Sales\\nRedwood Inference\\n",
    "From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>\\nTo: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com\\nDate: Sun, 30 May 2027 13:05:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Executive OKRs: headcount allocation checklist & freeze exceptions\\n\\nFinance check \u2014\\n\\nI reviewed Scenario B in the spreadsheet. Key notes:\\n- Hiring freeze baseline reduces OPEX by ~8% this fiscal year; each senior engineer adds ~1.15% to the variance under our model.\\n- Approving the Platform infra backfill + one senior infra hire pushes us over the comfortable variance threshold unless we de-prioritize two mid-tier reqs in Product.\\n- Proposed compromise: approve one critical backfill (Platform infra) immediately and stage the senior infra hire for Q4 conditional on measured latency improvements tied to the latency OKR.\\n\\nI've exported a short summary (cap_impact_summary.pdf). If Talent or Product has alternative comp assumptions, send them and I'll re-run.\\n\\nMarkus Klein\\nSVP, Finance\\nRedwood Inference\\n[Attachment: cap_impact_summary.pdf]\\n\\n> On Sun, 30 May 2027 at 11:18, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> > Adding Sales perspective \u2014\\n",
    "From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>\\nTo: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com\\nDate: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Executive OKRs: headcount allocation checklist & freeze exceptions\\n\\nAcked. I support the compromise Markus suggested \u2014 approve the Platform infra backfill now. For the senior infra hire, I want a short 6-week gate review with metrics: 95th latency improvement and incident reduction > 20% before unfreezing.\\n\\nVivek Kulkarni\\nDirector, Serving Runtime\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\n> On Sun, 30 May 2027 at 13:05, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> > Finance check \u2014\\n",
    "From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>\\nTo: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com\\nDate: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Executive OKRs: headcount allocation checklist & freeze exceptions\\n\\nThanks all \u2014 consolidation below (will be slide deck for Monday leadership sync):\\n\\nDecisions (agreed):\\n- Approve immediate backfill: Platform infra engineer (must-fill). Laura to open req and prioritize pipeline outreach.\\n- Freeze-exception required and approved process: freeze-exception-form.pdf to be completed for any non-backfill hires; exceptions will be reviewed weekly by execs.\\n- Senior infra hire: gated approval. Condition: 6-week gate with demonstrable latency/incident improvements. If metrics meet threshold, Finance to greenlight Q4 hire.\\n\\nAction items (owners & deadlines):\\n- Laura: post Platform infra backfill req; confirm 3 shortlisted candidates by 06/14. (Owner: laura_bennett)\\n- Marissa: finalize AE backfill priority and share ramp plan tied to ACME renewal by 06/07. (Owner: marissa_cole)\\n- Markus: rerun model with updated comp burdens if Talent changes assumptions; deliver updated cap_impact_summary by 06/08. (Owner: markus_klein)\\n- Vivek: provide the latency/incident target definition and measurement plan by 06/04 so Talent knows the hire gating criteria. (Owner: vivek_kulkarni)\\n- Michael: synthesize slide and circulate ahead of Monday leadership sync.\\n\\nI'll attach the consolidated slide to the calendar invite. Good work threading the trade-offs \u2014 this gives us a crisp recommendation for execs.\\n\\nMichael Grant\\nHead of Strategy & Ops\\nRedwood Inference\\n[Attachment: consolidated_headcount_slide.pdf (will attach to calendar invite)]\\n"

    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol\",\n  \"space\": \"applied-ml-and-evals\",\n  \"author\": \"Anjali Mehta\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-11-12\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2025-01-08\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Evan Park\",\n    \"Luis Ortega\",\n    \"Marina Cole\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"regression-triage\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"rollout-policy\",\n    \"probe-heatmap\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026\",\n    \"/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Summary\\n-------\\nThis document defines a reproducible protocol to convert probe heatmaps (telemetry-driven failure density views) into rollout decisions for model promotions, quantization migrations, and configuration changes. The goal is to make decisions auditable, time-bounded, and aligned with SLOs so product and ops can act consistently across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.\\n\\nScope\\n-----\\n- Applies to any promotion or rollout that is gated by probe-driven quality signals: model promotions, quantized rollouts, prompt rewrites, and routing policy changes.\\n- Focuses on probe heatmaps produced by the eval harness and live shadow probes (not human labelling pipelines).\\n- Excludes legislated/regulatory decisions (finance/compliance) - see separate compliance approval flow.\\n\\nKey definitions\\n---------------\\n- Probe heatmap: a time-windowed 2D histogram where rows are probes (slice identifiers) and columns are failure modes (fidelity, hallucination, latency, embeddings drift). Each cell contains count and a severity score.\\n- Decision score (DS): a normalized scalar computed from heatmap aggregates that maps to GO / CAUTION / HOLD / ROLLBACK actions.\\n- Tiered slice: pre-defined group of probes that share an SLO (e.g., CriticalTenantFlows, BillingIntents, LowRiskExplorations).\\n\\nInputs required\\n---------------\\n1) Heatmap snapshot covering the last N hours (default N=24) with per-probe metrics: total_calls, failure_count, avg_severity, median_latency_ms, embedding_drift_score.\\n2) Active rollout plan metadata: target model id, variant (quantized/float16), percent_traffic, scheduled_start.\\n3) Baseline reference heatmap from the control population (previous model or canary).\\n4) SLO manifest for target slices (SLO window, allowed error budget, latency SLO).\\n5) Operational constraints: maintenance windows, capacity headroom, and dependency map.\\n\\nDecision scoring algorithm (summary)\\n----------------------------------\\nWe compute three sub-scores and aggregate them into DS (range 0..100):\\n\\n- StabilityScore (SS): weighted failure density normalized by probe priority. Formula: SS = 100 * sum_p (w_p * (failure_count_p / max(1,total_calls_p))) / sum_p(w_p)\\n- LatencyPenalty (LP): 10 * max(0, (median_latency_ms - latency_slo_ms) / latency_slo_ms) clipped at 30\\n- DriftFactor (DF): 50 * embedding_drift_score_95pct_quantile normalized against baseline drift\\n\\nFinal Decision Score: DS = clamp(SS + LP + DF, 0, 100)\\n\\nAction mapping (recommended)\\n---------------------------\\n- DS <= 15: GO (promote / continue rollout)\\n- 15 < DS <= 35: CAUTION (slow rollout to 10% and schedule targeted human review within 4 hours)\\n- 35 < DS <= 60: HOLD (pause rollout; trigger automated bisect & focused probes)\\n- DS > 60: ROLLBACK (automatically revert to baseline variant and open incident ticket)\\n\\nConfiguration table (defaults)\\n-----------------------------\\n- heatmap_window_hours: 24 -- Time window to compute the snapshot\\n- probe_priority_weights: CriticalTenantFlows:10, BillingIntents:8, UXTextGen:3 -- Priority map used in SS\\n- latency_slo_ms: 250 -- latency SLO used for LP calculation\\n- drift_baseline_window_days: 7 -- Days used to compute baseline drift\\n- slow_roll_threshold: 35 -- DS threshold to switch to slow rollout\\n- human_review_timeout_hours: 4 -- Max time to complete targeted review\\n\\nOwnership and roles\\n-------------------\\n- Eval Oncall (primary): validates heatmap integrity, runs automated bisect and approves/requests human review.\\n- Model Owner (secondary): responsible for quick triage of failing slices and submitting patch/rollforward.\\n- Release Engineer: executes percent traffic adjustments and rollbacks in the serving control plane.\\n- Oncall Platform SRE: monitors capacity/latency regressions and authorizes emergency rollbacks for tail latency incidents.\\n\\nProcedure: from snapshot to decision (operational runbook)\\n------------------------------------------------------\\n1. Fetch heatmap snapshot and baseline. Verify telemetry completeness (missing probes < 5% of expected).\\n2. Run validation script to confirm probe schema and timestamps: 'python tools/heatmap_validate.py --snapshot /tmp/heatmap.json'\\n3. Compute DS using the scoring algorithm and emit a decision document to /incidents/probe-decisions/YYYYMMDD-HHMM.json. Example: curl -X POST 'https://ops-api.internal/decisions' -d '{'ds': 27, 'action': 'CAUTION', 'top_slices': ['BillingIntents:charge-failure'] }'\\n4. If action == GO: continue rollout. Log event and schedule a 24h follow-up check.\\n5. If action == CAUTION: cap rollout at 10% for 6 hours, assign Model Owner and Eval Oncall for targeted human validation, and run automated bisect on top 5 degrading slices.\\n6. If action == HOLD: pause rollout, mark the release as blocked in release tracker, and create a regression investigation ticket with pre-populated triage fields.\\n7. If action == ROLLBACK: trigger automated rollback playbook and notify the incident channel #regression-ops with summary and rollback links.\\n\\nAutomated bisect integration\\n---------------------------\\n- The decision pipeline calls the bisect service with the top N probes by (failure_count * avg_severity). The bisect run ID is included in the decision document.\\n- If bisect identifies a single suspect change (probability > 0.7) the Model Owner must decide to either patch or rollback within human_review_timeout_hours.\\n\\nTelemetry contract (minimal required fields)\\n-----------------------------------------\\nEmitters must provide a compact heatmap JSON with the following fields (example snippet):\\n\\n'{'\\n  'snapshot_ts': '2025-01-08T08:00:00Z',\\n  'window_hours': 24,\\n  'slices': [\\n    {\\n      'slice_id': 'BillingIntents:charge-failure',\\n      'total_calls': 12450,\\n      'failure_count': 312,\\n      'avg_severity': 2.8,\\n      'median_latency_ms': 430,\\n      'embedding_drift_score': 0.34\\n    }\\n  ]\\n}'\\n\\nRequired export fields (flat): snapshot_ts, window_hours, slices[].slice_id, slices[].total_calls, slices[].failure_count, slices[].avg_severity, slices[].median_latency_ms, slices[].embedding_drift_score. Optional: host_cluster, model_variant, tenant_id.\\n\\nSafety checks and hard gates\\n---------------------------\\n- If any CriticalTenantFlows slice has failure_rate > 0.5% AND avg_severity >= 3.0 the system must ROLLBACK regardless of DS.\\n- If more than 10% of probes lack current telemetry, mark decision state as INCONCLUSIVE and require human approval.\\n- For private/on-prem customers with per-customer SLO overrides, consult the customer SLO manifest before automatic rollback - use the per-customer override endpoint.\\n\\nRollback criteria and runbook steps\\n----------------------------------\\n1. Lock the rollout in the control plane: 'redwoodctl rollout lock --id <rollout-id>'\\n2. Execute the variant revert: 'redwoodctl rollout revert --id <rollout-id> --target <baseline-model>'\\n3. Post-rollback verification: run a 2-hour fast-probe sweep across top 20 slices and confirm DS falls below 20.\\n4. Create incident with severity mapping: DS>80 -> Sev2, DS 60-80 -> Sev3.\\n\\nExample: case study (short)\\n-------------------------\\n- Scenario: Quantized v1.2 was promoted to 20% across US-hosted tenants. After 12 hours heatmap snapshot showed elevated embedding_drift_score in 3 billing-related slices. Computed DS = 42 -> HOLD. Automated bisect pointed to a tokenizer change in the preprocessor. Model Owner rolled back quant patch and re-run priming probes; DS dropped to 12 within 3 hours and rollout resumed at a slow cadence.\\n\\nAppendix A: configuration YAML sample\\n------------------------------------\\n'heatmap_window_hours: 24\\nprobe_priority_weights:\\n  CriticalTenantFlows: 10\\n  BillingIntents: 8\\n  UXTextGen: 3\\nlatency_slo_ms: 250\\ndrift_baseline_window_days: 7\\nslow_roll_threshold: 35\\nhuman_review_timeout_hours: 4'\\n\\nAppendix B: links and references\\n--------------------------------\\n- Eval mesh and workload fingerprinting: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026\\n- Regression prioritization index: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024\\n\\nAppendix C: change history\\n--------------------------\\n- 2024-11-12 (Anjali Mehta): First draft and internal review.\\n- 2024-12-02 (Evan Park): Added bisect integration details and telemetry contract.\\n- 2025-01-08 (Marina Cole): Clarified safety gates for private deployments and updated example.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_b4bd83b46612452e858bc02b380082e2\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/probe-heatmap-rollout-decision-protocol-2024.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: applied-ml-and-evals\n\nscore.\n- Decision score (DS): a normalized scalar computed from heatmap aggregates that maps to GO / CAUTION / HOLD / ROLLBACK actions.\n- Tiered slice: pre-defined group of probes that share an SLO (e.g., CriticalTenantFlows, BillingIntents, LowRiskExplorations).\n\nInputs required\n---------------\n1) Heatmap snapshot covering the last N hours (default N=24) with per-probe metrics: total_calls, failure_count, avg_severity, median_latency_ms, embedding_drift_score.\n2) Active rollout plan metadata: target model id, variant (quantized/float16), percent_traffic, scheduled_start.\n3) Baseline reference heatmap from the control population (previous model or canary).\n4) SLO manifest for target slices (SLO window, allowed error budget, latency SLO).\n5) Operational constraints: maintenance windows, capacity headroom, and dependency map.\n\nDecision scoring algorithm (summary)\n----------------------------------\nWe compute three sub-scores and aggregate them into DS (range 0..100):\n\n- StabilityScore (SS): weighted failure density normalized by probe priority. Formula: SS = 100 * sum_p (w_p * (failure_count_p / max(1,total_calls_p))) / sum_p(w_p)\n- LatencyPenalty (LP): 10 * max(0, (median_latency_ms - latency_slo_ms) / latency_slo_ms) clipped at 30\n- DriftFactor (DF): 50 * embedding_drift_score_95pct_quantile normalized against baseline drift\n\nFinal Decision Score: DS = clamp(SS + LP + DF, 0, 100)\n\nAction mapping (recommended)\n---------------------------\n- DS <= 15: GO (promote / continue rollout)\n- 15 < DS <= 35: CAUTION (slow rollout to 10% and schedule targeted human review within 4 hours)\n- 35 < DS <= 60: HOLD (pause rollout; trigger automated bisect & focused probes)\n- DS > 60: ROLLBACK (automatically revert to baseline variant and open incident ticket)",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/probe-heatmap-rollout-decision-protocol-2024.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: applied-ml-and-evals\n\n35: CAUTION (slow rollout to 10% and schedule targeted human review within 4 hours)\n- 35 < DS <= 60: HOLD (pause rollout; trigger automated bisect & focused probes)\n- DS > 60: ROLLBACK (automatically revert to baseline variant and open incident ticket)\n\nConfiguration table (defaults)\n-----------------------------\n- heatmap_window_hours: 24 -- Time window to compute the snapshot\n- probe_priority_weights: CriticalTenantFlows:10, BillingIntents:8, UXTextGen:3 -- Priority map used in SS\n- latency_slo_ms: 250 -- latency SLO used for LP calculation\n- drift_baseline_window_days: 7 -- Days used to compute baseline drift\n- slow_roll_threshold: 35 -- DS threshold to switch to slow rollout\n- human_review_timeout_hours: 4 -- Max time to complete targeted review\n\nOwnership and roles\n-------------------\n- Eval Oncall (primary): validates heatmap integrity, runs automated bisect and approves/requests human review.\n- Model Owner (secondary): responsible for quick triage of failing slices and submitting patch/rollforward.\n- Release Engineer: executes percent traffic adjustments and rollbacks in the serving control plane.\n- Oncall Platform SRE: monitors capacity/latency regressions and authorizes emergency rollbacks for tail latency incidents.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/probe-heatmap-rollout-decision-protocol-2024.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: applied-ml-and-evals\n\n.\n- Model Owner (secondary): responsible for quick triage of failing slices and submitting patch/rollforward.\n- Release Engineer: executes percent traffic adjustments and rollbacks in the serving control plane.\n- Oncall Platform SRE: monitors capacity/latency regressions and authorizes emergency rollbacks for tail latency incidents.\n\nProcedure: from snapshot to decision (operational runbook)\n------------------------------------------------------\n1. Fetch heatmap snapshot and baseline. Verify telemetry completeness (missing probes < 5% of expected).\n2. Run validation script to confirm probe schema and timestamps: 'python tools/heatmap_validate.py --snapshot /tmp/heatmap.json'\n3. Compute DS using the scoring algorithm and emit a decision document to /incidents/probe-decisions/YYYYMMDD-HHMM.json. Example: curl -X POST 'https://ops-api.internal/decisions' -d '{'ds': 27, 'action': 'CAUTION', 'top_slices': ['BillingIntents:charge-failure'] }'\n4. If action == GO: continue rollout. Log event and schedule a 24h follow-up check.\n5. If action == CAUTION: cap rollout at 10% for 6 hours, assign Model Owner and Eval Oncall for targeted human validation, and run automated bisect on top 5 degrading slices.\n6. If action == HOLD: pause rollout, mark the release as blocked in release tracker, and create a regression investigation ticket with pre-populated triage fields.\n7. If action == ROLLBACK: trigger automated rollback playbook and notify the incident channel #regression-ops with summary and rollback links.\n\nAutomated bisect integration\n---------------------------\n- The decision pipeline calls the bisect service with the top N probes by (failure_count * avg_severity). The bisect run ID is included in the decision document.\n- If bisect identifies a single suspect change (probability > 0.7) the Model Owner must decide to either patch or rollback within human_review_timeout_hours.\n\nTelemetry contract (minimal required fields)\n-----------------------------------------\nEmitters must provide a compact heatmap JSON with the following fields (example snippet):",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/probe-heatmap-rollout-decision-protocol-2024.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: applied-ml-and-evals\n\nthe decision document.\n- If bisect identifies a single suspect change (probability > 0.7) the Model Owner must decide to either patch or rollback within human_review_timeout_hours.\n\nTelemetry contract (minimal required fields)\n-----------------------------------------\nEmitters must provide a compact heatmap JSON with the following fields (example snippet):\n\n'{'\n  'snapshot_ts': '2025-01-08T08:00:00Z',\n  'window_hours': 24,\n  'slices': [\n    {\n      'slice_id': 'BillingIntents:charge-failure',\n      'total_calls': 12450,\n      'failure_count': 312,\n      'avg_severity': 2.8,\n      'median_latency_ms': 430,\n      'embedding_drift_score': 0.34\n    }\n  ]\n}'\n\nRequired export fields (flat): snapshot_ts, window_hours, slices[].slice_id, slices[].total_calls, slices[].failure_count, slices[].avg_severity, slices[].median_latency_ms, slices[].embedding_drift_score. Optional: host_cluster, model_variant, tenant_id.\n\nSafety checks and hard gates\n---------------------------\n- If any CriticalTenantFlows slice has failure_rate > 0.5% AND avg_severity >= 3.0 the system must ROLLBACK regardless of DS.\n- If more than 10% of probes lack current telemetry, mark decision state as INCONCLUSIVE and require human approval.\n- For private/on-prem customers with per-customer SLO overrides, consult the customer SLO manifest before automatic rollback - use the per-customer override endpoint.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/probe-heatmap-rollout-decision-protocol-2024.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: applied-ml-and-evals\n\nOLLBACK regardless of DS.\n- If more than 10% of probes lack current telemetry, mark decision state as INCONCLUSIVE and require human approval.\n- For private/on-prem customers with per-customer SLO overrides, consult the customer SLO manifest before automatic rollback - use the per-customer override endpoint.\n\nRollback criteria and runbook steps\n----------------------------------\n1. Lock the rollout in the control plane: 'redwoodctl rollout lock --id <rollout-id>'\n2. Execute the variant revert: 'redwoodctl rollout revert --id <rollout-id> --target <baseline-model>'\n3. Post-rollback verification: run a 2-hour fast-probe sweep across top 20 slices and confirm DS falls below 20.\n4. Create incident with severity mapping: DS>80 -> Sev2, DS 60-80 -> Sev3.\n\nExample: case study (short)\n-------------------------\n- Scenario: Quantized v1.2 was promoted to 20% across US-hosted tenants. After 12 hours heatmap snapshot showed elevated embedding_drift_score in 3 billing-related slices. Computed DS = 42 -> HOLD. Automated bisect pointed to a tokenizer change in the preprocessor. Model Owner rolled back quant patch and re-run priming probes; DS dropped to 12 within 3 hours and rollout resumed at a slow cadence.\n\nAppendix A: configuration YAML sample\n------------------------------------\n'heatmap_window_hours: 24\nprobe_priority_weights:\n  CriticalTenantFlows: 10\n  BillingIntents: 8\n  UXTextGen: 3\nlatency_slo_ms: 250\ndrift_baseline_window_days: 7\nslow_roll_threshold: 35\nhuman_review_timeout_hours: 4'\n\nAppendix B: links and references\n--------------------------------\n- Eval mesh and workload fingerprinting: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026\n- Regression prioritization index: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024",
